records.title: Values
records.content:
These are not qualities I possess perfectly. They are things I try to
return to when deciding how to live and work.

- **Focus.** Choose a small number of things that matter and keep returning my attention to them.
- **Health.** Protect the physical and mental stability that makes everything else possible.
- **Thoughtful openness.** Listen seriously to other people without
  giving up the responsibility to think for myself.
- **Speaking when it matters.** Important things should be said clearly,
  even when I am inclined to remain quiet.
- **Adaptability.** Change my mind, plans, and methods when circumstances or evidence change.
- **Respect.** Try to understand people before judging them and treat their perspectives as real.
- **Generosity.** Share useful knowledge, attention, and help when I can.
- **Forward movement.** Take the next concrete step instead of waiting to become a different kind of person.

records.title: Adelic and Classical Modular Forms for GL(2)
records.summary: Adelic and Classical Modular Forms for GL(2). An exposition of the translation between classical modular forms and automorphic forms on the adelic group $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{A}_{\mathbb{Q}})$. Provides a geometric interpretation of modular forms as sections of line bundles over modular curves, along with minimal ad hoc constructions of Eisenstein series. Details the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{gl}_2(\mathbb{R})$ with basis elements $Z, H, Y_+, Y_-$, where the center $\mathcal{Z}(\mathfrak{gl}_2)$ of the universal enveloping algebra is isomorphic to a polynomial ring in two generators. Explores the space of bases $B$ of $\mathbb{C}$ as a real vector space, identifying it as an open subset of $\mathbb{C}^2$ with commuting left and right actions by $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ and $\mathrm{GL}_1(\mathbb{C})$. The right action of $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ is complex analytic and gives an identification with the upper half-plane $\mathcal{H}^{\pm} \times \mathbb{C}^\times$ via $(\tau, z) \mapsto \left(\frac{a\tau+c}{b\tau+d}, (b\tau+d)z\right)$. Examines the complexified Lie algebra tangent space decomposition into holomorphic and anti-holomorphic subspaces, the subspace $V_i \subset \mathfrak{gl}_2$, and the bijection $B/\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{Z}) \cong \mathcal{L}$ with the moduli of discrete rank-2 lattices. Covers moderate growth conditions, smooth adelic automorphic forms, and representations invariant under right translation by $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{A}_f)$.

records.title: Class Field Theory and Noncommutative Geometry
records.summary: Class Field Theory and Noncommutative Geometry. An exposition by Alain Connes on class field theory through the lens of the adèle class space $X_{\mathbb{Q}} = \mathbb{Q}^\times \backslash \mathbb{A}_{\mathbb{Q}}$. Abelian extensions of a number field $K$ are encoded internally by its idele class group $C_K = \mathbb{A}_K^\times / K^\times$, acting as a Galois group of the maximal abelian extension via Artin reciprocity. Galois actions on roots are realized through group actions on spaces. The quotient space $X_K = K^\times \backslash \mathbb{A}_K$ is ergodic with respect to the Haar measure, serving as a prototype noncommutative space (leaf space of a foliation). Translates local-to-global class field theory via the inclusion of local isotropy groups $K_v^\times \hookrightarrow C_K$. Connects the Riemann–Weil explicit formulas $\sum_v \int f(u)/|1-u|\,d^*u$ to a trace formula for the scaling operator on the adèle class space. Introduces the scaling site $X_{\mathbb{Q}} = \mathbb{Q}^\times \backslash \mathbb{A}_{\mathbb{Q}} / \widehat{\mathbb{Z}}^\times$, modeled as a noncommutative space of rank-1 subgroups of $\mathbb{R}$, where periodic orbits of length $\log p$ correspond to prime numbers $p$, realizing the Frobenius endomorphism as a mapping torus. Relates this construction to Grothendieck's étale fundamental group $\pi_1^{\text{ét}}$ and the 3D topology of $\operatorname{Spec} \mathbb{Z}$.

records.title: Maximal Abelian Extensions Unramified Outside S
records.summary: Maximal Abelian Extensions Unramified Outside S. Discussion and computation of the maximal abelian extension $K_S^{\text{ab}}$ of a number field $K$ unramified outside a finite set of places $S$. For a singleton prime $S = \{p\}$, $K_S^{\text{ab}}$ is given by the direct limit of ray class fields modulo $\mathfrak{p}^n \mathcal{O}_K$. Explains ramification at infinite places and the Galois group $G_S(K)^{\text{ab}} = G_S(K) / \overline{[G_S(K), G_S(K)]}$. Details the connection to class field theory, Poitou–Tate duality, and the Kronecker–Weber theorem for $K = \mathbb{Q}$.

records.title: The Six-Functor Formalism on Infinity-Categories
records.summary: The Six-Functor Formalism on Infinity-Categories. Scholze's paper establishing the six-functor formalism as a lax symmetric monoidal functor from a category of correspondences $\operatorname{Corr}(\mathcal{C}, E)$ to $\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$. Formulates pushforward $f_*$, proper pushforward $f_!$, pullback $f^*$, exceptional pullback $f^!$, tensor product $\otimes$, and internal $\operatorname{\mathcal{R}Hom}$. Deduces proper base change and the projection formula $f_!(A \otimes f^*B) \cong f_!(A) \otimes B$ using Lurie's straightening/unstraightening for Cartesian fibrations over $\operatorname{Fin}_*$. Discusses cohomological smoothness, local Verdier duality, and base change for rigid-analytic and perfectoid spaces.

records.title: Comprehensive Glossary of Algebraic Geometry
records.summary:
Comprehensive Glossary of Algebraic Geometry. A 46-page reference dictionary compiling core definitions and theorems:
- **Abelian Categories & Additivity:** Categories equipped with biproducts $\bigoplus$, kernels, cokernels, and the first isomorphism theorem $\operatorname{Coim}(f) \cong \operatorname{Im}(f)$. Semiadditive categories satisfy $\coprod \cong \prod$, yielding semiring structures on endomorphism sets $\operatorname{End}(X)$.
- **Ampleness & Positivity:** A line bundle $\mathcal{L}$ on a projective scheme $X$ is very ample if it admits a closed immersion $X \hookrightarrow \mathbb{P}_A^n$ defined by global sections; ample if $\mathcal{L}^{\otimes m}$ is very ample for some $m > 0$. Base-point freeness means global sections generate the stalks $\mathcal{L}_x$ everywhere.
- **Divisors & Canonical Sheaves:** Cartier divisors are global sections of $\mathcal{K}_X^\times / \mathcal{O}_X^\times$. Weil divisors $\sum n_i Y_i$ are formal integer linear combinations of codimension-1 prime subvarieties. The canonical bundle $\omega_X = \det(\Omega_{X/k}^1)$ is the top exterior power of Kähler differentials, acting as the dualizing sheaf in Serre duality.
- **Morphisms & Flatness:** Flat morphisms preserve exact sequences under tensor products $\mathcal{F} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_Y} \mathcal{O}_X$, ensuring constant Hilbert polynomials across fibers. Étale morphisms are smooth of relative dimension 0 (flat and unramified). Proper morphisms are separated, finite type, and universally closed.
- **Cohomology & Derived Functors:** Sheaf cohomology groups $H^i(X, \mathcal{F}) = R^i\Gamma(X, \mathcal{F})$ quantify obstructions to gluing local sections into global ones. Flasque and soft sheaves are acyclic, computing Čech cohomology without higher derived corrections.

records.title: Internal Language of Topoi in Algebraic Geometry
records.summary:
Internal Language of Topoi in Algebraic Geometry. Ingo Blechschmidt's slides on the petit and gros Zariski topoi:
- **Petit Zariski Topos $\operatorname{Shv}(X)$:** The structure sheaf $\mathcal{O}_X$ internally behaves as a field (or local ring where every non-invertible element is nilpotent). A sheaf of modules $\mathcal{F}$ is locally of finite type if and only if it is internally finitely generated. Coherent sheaves correspond internally to finitely presented modules.
- **Gros Zariski Topos $\operatorname{Zar}(S)$:** Represents schemes by their functors of points $\mathbf{Sch}/S \to \mathbf{Set}$. The affine line $\mathbb{A}^1$ behaves internally as a commutative field where every function $\mathbb{A}^1 \to \mathbb{A}^1$ is a polynomial. Group schemes $\mathbb{G}_a, \mathbb{G}_m, \mathrm{GL}_n$ appear internally as standard algebraic groups.

- **Quantum Mechanics & Uncertainty:** Noncommuting variables $[P, Q] = i\hbar$, spectral geometry, Dirac operators as square roots of Laplacians, and Dixmier traces.

records.title: Noncommutative Geometry and Fundamental Physics
records.summary:
Noncommutative Geometry and Fundamental Physics. Alain Connes' landmark survey detailing:
- **Quantum Variables:** Real variables correspond to self-adjoint operators in Hilbert space; infinitesimals correspond to compact operators.
- **Metric Structures:** Distance formula $d(p, q) = \sup \{|f(p) - f(q)| : \|[D, f]\| \le 1\}$, where the line element $ds = D^{-1}$ is the fermion propagator.
- **Thermodynamics & Time:** Noncommutativity implies a canonical 1-parameter automorphism group $\delta_t \in \operatorname{Out}(\mathcal{A})$ via the Tomita–Takesaki KMS condition.
- **Bost-Connes System:** Exhibits spontaneous symmetry breaking at critical temperature $\beta = 1$ with the Riemann zeta function $\zeta(\beta)$ as the partition function.

records.title: Geometry of the Adele Class Space: Part I
records.summary:
Geometry of the Adele Class Space: Part I. Alain Connes' lecture exploring:
- **Number Fields & Schemes:** Unifying number rings $\mathcal{O}_K$, function fields $\mathbb{F}_q(C)$, and Riemann surfaces as 1-dimensional regular schemes.
- **Galois Theory & Etale Topology:** Separable algebras, traces, finite étale morphisms, and why $\operatorname{Spec} \mathbb{Z}$ behaves as a simply connected 3-manifold where primes are knots.
- **Topos Semantics:** Topoi allow groups/monoids to act naturally. The topos $([0, \infty) \rtimes \mathbb{N}^\times)$ computes points over the Boolean semifield $\mathbb{B} = \{0,1\}$, recovering the adèle class space.

- **Galois Theory & Etale Topology:** Separable algebras, traces, finite étale morphisms, and why $\operatorname{Spec} \mathbb{Z}$ behaves as a simply connected 3-manifold where primes are knots.
- **Topos Semantics:** Topoi allow groups/monoids to act naturally. The topos $([0, \infty) \rtimes \mathbb{N}^\times)$ computes points over the Boolean semifield $\mathbb{B} = \{0,1\}$, recovering the adèle class space.

records.title: Geometry of the Adele Class Space: Part II
records.summary:
Geometry of the Adele Class Space: Part II. Alain Connes' second lecture:
- **Adèles & Global Fields:** Global fields sit discretely and cocompactly in their locally compact adèle rings $\mathbb{A}_K$.
- **Trace Formulas & Absorption Spectra:** The scaling action on $K_v$ has Schwartz kernel $\delta(y - \lambda x)$ with trace $\int \delta(x - \lambda x)\,dx = 1/|1-\lambda|$. Zeros of $L$-functions emerge as an absorption spectrum, explaining the minus sign in explicit formulas.
- **The Arithmetic Site:** The topos $(\mathbb{N}^\times, \mathbb{Z}_{\max})$ over the tropical semifield $\mathbb{R}_{\max}$ exhibits Frobenius automorphisms $\operatorname{Fr}_\lambda(x) = x^\lambda$, establishing an explicit Riemann–Roch theorem for number fields.

records.title: Commutative Algebra in the Stacks Project
records.summary:
Commutative Algebra in the Stacks Project. The foundational 1000+ page reference on commutative algebra:
- **Exact Sequences & Finiteness:** Snake lemma connecting homomorphisms, finite presentation criteria, and flatness via Tor vanishing.
- **Localizations & Spectra:** Universal property of localizations $S^{-1}R$, prime avoidance, the Zariski spectrum $\operatorname{Spec}(R)$, and characterization of minimal primes as irreducible components.
- **Dimension & Regularity:** Krull dimension, Cohen–Macaulay rings where homological depth equals Krull dimension, and regular local rings ($\dim R = \dim_{\kappa} \mathfrak{m}/\mathfrak{m}^2$).
- **Differentials & Smoothness:** Modules of Kähler differentials $\Omega_{S/R}^1$, the de Rham complex, formally smooth/unramified/étale ring morphisms, and Henselian local rings.

records.title: Category Theory in Context
records.summary:
Category Theory in Context. Emily Riehl's foundational textbook covering:
- **Preservation, Reflection, Creation:** Functors preserve limits (limit in domain $\implies$ limit in codomain), reflect limits (limit cone in image $\implies$ limit cone in domain), and create limits (limit in codomain $\implies$ unique limit lifting).
- **Kan Extensions:** Left Kan extensions $\operatorname{Lan}_K F$ (generalizing colimits) and right Kan extensions $\operatorname{Ran}_K F$ (generalizing limits). Pointwise Kan extensions are computed via limit formulas over comma categories: $\operatorname{Ran}_K F(d) \cong \lim (d/K \to \mathcal{C} \to \mathcal{E})$.
- **Yoneda & Density:** The Yoneda lemma as a pointwise Kan extension. The co-Yoneda lemma expresses every presheaf as a colimit of representables: $F(c) \cong \operatorname{colim}(\mathcal{C}/c \to \mathcal{C} \to \mathbf{Set})$.
- **Codensity Monads:** The right Kan extension of a functor along itself. The codensity monad of $\mathbf{FinSet} \hookrightarrow \mathbf{Set}$ is the ultrafilter monad.

records.title: Yi Yu Zhang
records.summary: Yi Yu Zhang, Introduction to equivariant cohomology and the equivariant first Chern class. The goal of this paper to provide a relatively accessible and integrated introduction to the algebraic topology of spaces with Lie group actions, in both the smooth and the holomorphic category. We present detailed treatment of the basic constructions in equivariant de Rham theory and Dolbeault theory. We also discuss equivariant connections and curvature on vector bundles equipped with infinitesimal lifts, as well as the equivariant first Chern class of line bundles with inﬁnitesimal lifts. A novel feature of this presentation is the deﬁnition of infinitesimal lift via differential operators on the vector bundles.

records.summary: Arthur-César Le Bras, prismatic Dieudonné theory classifies $p$-divisible groups via filtered prismatic Dieudonné crystals. records.title: Jeffrey Lambie-Hanson (joint with Chris Lambie-Hanson)
records.summary: Jeffrey Lambie-Hanson (joint with Chris Lambie-Hanson), infinitary combinatorics in condensed mathematics and strong homology. Key computation: for $X^{n,\lambda}$ the one-point compactification of a disjoint sum of $\lambda$ copies of the open $n$-ball, $\bar H_p(\bigvee_\omega X^{n,\lambda})=\bigoplus_\omega \bar H_p(X^{n,\lambda})$ iff $\lim^{n-p} A^{\omega}_\lambda=0$, where $A^\kappa_\lambda=\langle\prod_{I(f)}\mathbb Z\rangle$ is the inverse system attached to $f:\kappa\to[\lambda]^{<\omega}$, generalizing Mardešić–Prasolov's criterion; forcing with Hechler or $\beth_\omega$-many Laver reals kills all $\lim^n A[H]$ (yielding $2^{\aleph_0}>\aleph_\omega$ via Casarosa–Lambie-Hanson), making strong homology additive on locally compact separable metric spaces and embedding separable pro-abelian groups fully faithfully in $\mathrm{Cond}(\mathrm{Ab})$; in ZFC the uncountable earring space and $\prod_\omega\prod_{\omega_1}\mathbb{Z}$ give counterexamples, so nonseparable condensed behavior is provably bad.

records.summary: Guozhen Wang, topological cyclic homology of local fields via a descent spectral sequence built from a prismatic/Dieudonné-type $\delta$-ring structure. Key computation: for a local field $K$ with ring of integers $O_K$ and uniformizer $\varpi$, computes relative $THH(O_K/S\langle z\rangle)$ for $S\langle z\rangle=\mathbb{Z}_p[z]$, $z\mapsto\varpi$; the filtration by the fiber of $\mathrm{can}-\varphi$ gives $E_1^{i,j}\Rightarrow TC_{i+j}(O_K)$, and the $E_2$-term of the descent spectral sequence for $TP(O_K)$ is computed as $\mathrm{Ext}$ of the Hopf algebroid $(TP_0(O_K/S[z_0,z_1]), TP_0(O_K/S[z_0,z_0,z_1]))$, with $TP_0(O_K/S[z_0,z_1])$ the Nygaard-completion of a $\delta$-ring generated by $h=\varphi(E)^{-1}\sigma$-type elements.

records.title: Albert Jinghui Yang
records.summary: Albert Jinghui Yang, topological cyclic homology of local fields via secondary spectral sequences on the Nygaard filtration. Key computation: the descent spectral sequence for $TC(O_K)$ is obtained by filtering by the fiber of $\mathrm{can}-\varphi$ levelwise, $E_1^{i,j}\Rightarrow TC_{i+j}(O_K\otimes\mathbb{Z}_p^t\text{-terms})$; the Nygaard filtration $N^{\geq j}$ on the $E_1$-terms of the descent spectral sequence for $TC^-$ and $TP$ produces secondary spectral sequences, e.g. $E_2^{1}(TC^-)=H^i(\mathrm{gr}^{2k}_{TC^-(O_K/S\otimes[n])})\Rightarrow E_2^2(TC^-)$, connecting Nygaard-complete $\delta$-ring data to explicit $TC$-groups.

records.title: Chrysanthemum (Chang)
records.summary: Chrysanthemum (Chang), introduction to prismatic cohomology identifying it with derived de Rham cohomology. Key computation: for a quasi-syntomic ring $R$, after $p$-completion there is a canonical quasi-isomorphism $q\Omega^*_{R/\mathbb{Z}_p}\simeq \Delta_R$ over the base prism $(\mathbb{Z}_p,p)$, resolving a conjecture; the Hodge–Tate comparison gives $\mathrm{gr}^i\bar\Delta_R \cong \bar\Omega^i_R[i]$, and the Nygaard filtration on $TC^-$ recovers the motivic filtration.

records.title: Huan–Young
records.summary: Huan–Young, twisted Real quasi-elliptic cohomology realized as a twist of Tate K-theory. Key computation: twisted Real quasi-elliptic cohomology $QEll_H^*(X)$ comes with explicit restriction $K_G^*(X)\to QEll_H^*(X)$, induction $QEll_H^*(X)\to K_H^*(X)$, and Künneth $QEll_G^*(X)\hat\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm}]} QEll_H^*(Y)\to QEll_{G\times H}^*(X\times Y)$ maps; a change-of-group isomorphism $QEll_G^*(Y\times_H G)\cong QEll_H^*(Y)$ and a transfer map $K_{\Sigma_N}^*(pt)\to K^*(pt)/I_{tr}$ with explicit transfer ideal $I_{tr}^{\mathrm{Tate}}$ complete the picture.

records.title: Bin Zhao
records.summary: Bin Zhao, slopes of modular forms and the ghost conjecture. Key computation: for normalized $f\in S_k(\Gamma_1(N))$ with $p\mid N$, the slope of $f$ is $v_p(a_p)$ for the $U_p$-eigenvalue $a_p$; a ghost map built from the ghost components of a Witt-vector-like ring on the space of modular forms gives an algorithm computing the Newton slopes of $U_p$, and the ghost conjecture (Buzzard) states this ghost map computes slopes exactly, verified in explicit slope tables for small $p,N$.

records.title: Zhang
records.summary: Zhang, a Quillen–Lichtenbaum conjecture for Dirichlet $L$-functions. Key computation: reformulates Dirichlet's unit theorem $\mathcal{O}_F^\times\cong\mu(F)\times\mathbb{Z}^{\oplus r_1+r_2-1}$ (so $\dim_\mathbb{Q}\mathcal{O}_F^\times\otimes\mathbb{Q}=\mathrm{ord}_{s=0}\zeta_F(s)$) and the class number formula $\zeta_F^*(0)=-\frac{|cl(F)|}{|\mu(F)|}R(F)$ via $K_0(\mathcal{O}_F)\cong\mathbb{Z}\oplus cl(F)$ and $K_1(\mathcal{O}_F)\cong\mathcal{O}_F^\times$, then states/proves a Quillen–Lichtenbaum-type statement identifying rational equivariant algebraic K-groups of number fields with values of Dirichlet $L$-functions at nonpositive integers.

records.title: Xintong Gu
records.summary: Xintong Gu, ordinary and motivic cohomology of $BPGL_n(\mathbb{C})$. Key computation: motivic cohomology satisfies $\tilde{H}M^{s,s}(\mathrm{spec}(k),A)\cong K_M^s(k)\otimes A$ (Milnor K-theory) and $\mathbb{A}^1$-homotopy invariance $H_M^{*,*}(X\times\mathbb{A}^1)\cong H_M^{*,*}(X)$; computes the motivic cohomology of the classifying stack $BPGL_n$ via the sites $\mathrm{Torsor}_{Nis}(-)\to H_M^{*,*}(-,B_{Nis}G)$ and $\mathrm{Torsor}_{\acute{e}t}(-)\to H_M^{*,*}(-,B_{\acute{e}t}G)$, classifying $G$-torsors and giving explicit $H^{*,*}(BPGL_n)$-calculations.

records.title: Si-Ying Lee
records.summary: Si-Ying Lee, prismatic Dieudonné theory generalizing Breuil–Kisin's classification of $p$-divisible groups. Key computation: reduces good reduction of $p$-divisible groups $G=A_{\mathbb{Z}}[p^\infty]$ to $T_pG$ being crystalline (the proved Fontaine conjecture), via Breuil–Kisin's fully faithful functor $\mathrm{Rep}_{\mathcal{O}_K^{ur}}(\mathrm{Gal}_k)\to\{\text{Breuil–Kisin modules}\}$ and $BT/\mathcal{O}_K\simeq\{\text{subcat. of BK-modules}\}$, generalized by Bhatt–Scholze's prismatic F-crystals; for a $p$-divisible group $G/X$, $\mathrm{Ext}^2_{X/S}(\underline{G},0)=0$ and $\mathrm{Ext}^1_{X/S}(\underline{G},0)\simeq\mathrm{Im}(\mathrm{Ext}^1(\underline{G}_{n+m},0)\to\mathrm{Ext}^1(\underline{G}_n,0))$ is locally free of rank $2kh/\mathcal{O}_T$, computed via the snake lemma on $0\to\underline{G}_n\to\underline{G}\xrightarrow{p^n}\underline{G}\to0$.

records.title: Avi Zeff
records.summary: Avi Zeff, overview of prismatic cohomology and its comparison theorems. Key computation: for a perfect prism $(A,(d))$ with $R=A/d$ perfectoid, the étale comparison identifies nearby cycles $R\mu_*\mathbb{Z}/p^n \simeq (\Delta_{X/A}[1/d]/p^n)^{\varphi=1}$; the Hodge–Tate comparison shows $\Delta_{X/A}$ is a perfect complex with $\mathrm{gr}^i \simeq \Omega^i_{X/(A/I)}[-i]$ via reduction to characteristic $p$ and the Cartier isomorphism; and the Nygaard filtration $\mathrm{Fil}_i^N A := \{x\in A : \varphi(x)\in d^i A\}$ lifts the Hodge filtration via $d^{\varphi(i)}$-twisted maps.

records.title: Bhargav Bhatt
records.summary: Bhargav Bhatt, derived prismatic cohomology extended to arbitrary $p$-complete $A/I$-algebras via non-abelian derived functors. Key computation: for a regular semiperfect $k$-algebra $S=R/I$ with $R$ perfect over $k$ and $I$ generated by a regular sequence, $L_{S/R} \simeq I/I^2[1]$ and $\wedge^i L_{S/R} \simeq \Gamma_i^R(I/I^2)[i]$; the conjugate filtration forces $dR_{S/k}^\infty$ to be concentrated in degree $0$ and equal $D_I^\infty(R)$ — e.g. $S=k[x^{1/p^\infty}]/(x)$ gives $dR_{S/k}^\infty \simeq \bigoplus_{i\in\mathbb{N}[1/p]} k\cdot x^i/\lfloor i\rfloor!$ — and descending along the Čech nerve of $R\to R_{perf}$ computes $dR_{R/k}$ for smooth $R$.

records.title: Bhargav Bhatt
records.summary: Bhargav Bhatt, the prismatic site $(R/A)_\Delta$ and the Hodge–Tate comparison theorem. Key computation: for the torus $R=(\mathcal{O}_K[X^{\pm1}])^\wedge$ over the base prism $(A,I)=(\mathbb{Z}_p\langle q-1\rangle,([p]_q))$ with $[i]_q=(q^i-1)/(q-1)$, $\bar\Delta_{R/A}$ is computed by the two-term $q$-de Rham complex $A\langle X^{\pm1}\rangle \xrightarrow{[i]_q\frac{dX}{X}} A\langle X^{\pm1}\rangle$; since $[i]_q$ is invertible mod $[p]_q$ for $p\nmid i$ and $[kp]_q=0$, reduction mod $[p]_q$ yields the graded pieces $H^0=\bigoplus_i (A/I)X^{kp}$, $H^1=\bigoplus_i (A/I)X^{kp}\frac{dX}{X}$, explicitly verifying the Hodge–Tate isomorphism $\Omega^*_{R/(A/I)}\cong H^*(\bar\Delta_{R/A})$ and perfectness of $\bar\Delta_{R/A}$.

records.title: Rizzo
records.summary: Rizzo, condensed mathematics and analytic geometry classifying classical topological categories by separatedness conditions on condensed sets. Key computation: Theorem 1.1.15 shows the category $\mathrm{Top}^\omega$ of compactly generated topological spaces is equivalent to quasi-separated condensed sets; light profinite sets are exactly quotients of the Cantor set $\{0,1\}^{\mathbb{N}}$, and extremally disconnected profinite sets give internally projective $\mathbb{Z}[S]$, proving $\mathrm{Cond}(\mathrm{Ab})$ is abelian with enough projectives.

records.title: Xinyu Zhou
records.summary: Xinyu Zhou, prismatic cohomology as cohomology of the structure sheaf on the relative prismatic site, comparing to classical $p$-adic cohomology theories without smoothness/properness. Key computation: for a bounded prism $(A,I)$ and smooth $p$-adic formal $X/\mathrm{Spf}\,A/I$, the crystalline case $I=(p)$ gives $R\Gamma_{\mathrm{crys}}(X/A)\simeq R\Gamma_\Delta(X/A)\otimes^L_{A,\varphi_A}A$; the de Rham comparison gives $H^i(R\Gamma_\Delta(X/A)\otimes^L_A A/I)\simeq\Omega^i_{R/(A/I)}\{-i\}$ with Nygaard twist $\{-i\}=-(I/I^2)^{\otimes i}$; the étale comparison for perfect $A$ gives $R\Gamma_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X_\eta,\mathbb{Z}/p^n)\simeq R\Gamma_\Delta(X/A)\otimes^L_A(A/p)[1/I]$; and the functor $R\mapsto(A_{\mathrm{inf}}(R),\ker\theta)$ gives an equivalence perfect prisms $\simeq$ perfectoid rings.

records.title: Peter Scholze
records.summary: Peter Scholze, perfectoid spaces as a framework for almost purity and weight-monodromy via tilting between mixed and equal characteristic. Key computation: classification of points of the adic space $\mathrm{Spa}(R,R^+)$ over $k=\langle T\rangle$: the functor $r:X\mapsto X^{ad}$ induces an equivalence $\{$qs rigid-analytic varieties$/k\}\cong\{$qs adic spaces locally of finite type$/k\}$, and the five types of points are classified — closed rank-1 points, branching points of type 2 with the Gauß point, type-3 points from a disc $D(x,r)$, dead ends from nested discs $D_1\supset D_2\supset\cdots$ with empty intersection (existing iff $k$ is not spherically complete), and rank-2 points with value group $\Gamma=\mathbb{R}_{>0}\times\gamma^{\mathbb{Z}}$.

records.title: Peter Scholze
records.summary: Peter Scholze, perfectoid spaces and their applications: tilting/untilting and the Fargues–Fontaine curve. Key computation: Theorem 3.3 — for a perfectoid field $K$ with tilt $K^\flat$, $L\mapsto L^\flat$ gives an equivalence between finite extensions of $K$ and of $K^\flat$, hence an isomorphism $G_K\cong G_{K^\flat}$; Theorem 4.1 (Fargues–Fontaine) — for a perfectoid field $L$ of characteristic $p$ there is a regular noetherian scheme $X_L$ of Krull dimension 1 over $\mathbb{Q}_p$ whose closed points are in bijection with equivalence classes of untilts $(K,\iota:L\to K^\flat)$ up to $\iota\circ\Phi^n$, of degree $[K^\flat:L]$.

records.title: Bhargav Bhatt
records.summary: Bhargav Bhatt, overview lecture on prismatic cohomology unifying integral $p$-adic cohomology theories. Key computation: Theorem 3.3 attaches to $R$ a $(p,u)$-adically complete complex $\Delta_{R/A}$ with Frobenius $\varphi_{R/A}:\varphi^*\Delta_{R/A}\to\Delta_{R/A}$ satisfying $\varphi^*\Delta_{R/A}\otimes^L_A \mathbb{F}_p \simeq \Omega^*_{R_{\mathbb{F}_p}/\mathbb{F}_p}$ (crystalline comparison), $\Delta_{R/A}\otimes^L_A \mathbb{F}_p((u))$ with $\varphi=1$ fixed points $\simeq R\Gamma_{\text{ét}}(\mathrm{Spec}\,R_C,\mathbb{F}_p)$ (étale comparison), and $H^i(\Delta_{R/A}\otimes^L_A \mathbb{Z}_p)\simeq\Omega^i_{R/\mathbb{Z}_p}$ (de Rham comparison); for $R$ the completion of $\mathbb{Z}[x,x^{-1}]$, $\Omega^*_{R/\mathbb{Z}_p}=\bigoplus_{i\in\mathbb{Z}}\mathbb{Z}_p\cdot x^i(dx/x)\to \mathbb{Z}_p\cdot x^i$ computes the torus example.

records.title: Peter Scholze
records.summary: Peter Scholze, prisms and prismatic cohomology. Key computation: Theorem 1.8 — for a bounded prism $(A,I)$ and smooth $p$-adic formal $X/\mathrm{Spf}(A/I)$, $\mathrm{can}\otimes\varphi: \varphi^*R\Gamma_\Delta(X/A)\otimes^L_A A[1/I]\simeq R\Gamma_{\mathrm{crys}}(X/A)$, and the Hodge–Tate comparison gives $\Omega^i_{R/(A/I)}\{-i\}\simeq H^i(R\Gamma_\Delta(X/A)\otimes^L_A A/I)$ with Tate twist $\{-i\}=(I/I^2)^{\otimes i}$; over the $q$-prism $(\mathbb{Z}_p\langle q-1\rangle,([p]_q))$ with $[p]_q=(q^p-1)/(q-1)$, prismatic cohomology recovers the $q$-de Rham complexes, and the Nygaard filtration is $F^iA=\{x\in A:\varphi(x)\in d^iA\}$.

records.title: Jacob Lurie
records.summary: Jacob Lurie, foundations of perfectoid spaces and the tilting correspondence for integral perfectoid rings. Key computation: Theorem 1.7 — for integral perfectoid $A$, $B\mapsto B^\flat$ is an equivalence $\{$integral perfectoid $A$-algebras$\}\cong\{$integral perfectoid $A^\flat$-algebras$\}$ with inverse $C\mapsto C^\#=W(C)\otimes_{W(A^\flat),\theta}A$, compatible with almost isomorphisms; Proposition 1.6 constructs $\theta:W(A^\flat)\to A$ with kernel generated by $\xi=p+[\pi^\flat]^px$, and the divisibility computation $\pi^{p^l}a^p\in\pi^pA\Rightarrow\pi^la\in\pi A$ shows $\xi$ is a non-zero-divisor.

records.title: Kiran Kedlaya
records.summary: Kiran Kedlaya, a brief history of perfectoid spaces. Key computation: the Fontaine–Wintenberger field-of-norms isomorphism between the absolute Galois groups of $\mathbb{Q}_p(\zeta_{p^\infty})$ and $\mathbb{F}_p((\pi))$ is, in retrospect, the first tilting equivalence between perfectoid spaces; the slides trace the period ring construction $B^+(L)$ as the completion of $W(O_L)[1/p]$ and its role in parametrizing untilts.

records.title: Jared Weinstein
records.summary: Jared Weinstein, adic spaces for perfectoid geometry. Key computation: Theorem 2.3.2 — the map $I\mapsto(W(K^\circ)/I)[1/p]$ is a bijection between degree-1 primitive ideals of $W(K^\circ)$ and isomorphism classes of untilts of the perfectoid field $K$ ($I=(p)$ giving the trivial untilt); Theorem 2.3.5 (FF11) — for algebraically closed $C$ the closed maximal ideals of $B_C$ parametrize untilts, and $X_K=Y_K/\varphi^{\mathbb{Z}}$ with $Y_K=\mathrm{Spa}(W(K^\circ))\setminus\{|p[\omega]|=0\}$ is the Fargues–Fontaine curve.

records.title: Dominic Joyce
records.summary: Dominic Joyce, derived algebraic geometry background lectures. Key computation: derived Bézout — for projective curves $C,D\subset\mathbb{CP}^2$ of degrees $m,n$, the derived intersection $C\cap D$ is a proper quasi-smooth derived scheme with $\mathrm{vdim}=0$ and virtual count $[X]^{\mathrm{virt}}=mn$ even when $\dim X=1$; the cdga model $A^*=\mathbb{C}[x_1..x_m;y_1..y_n]$ with $dy_i=p_i$ gives $H^0=\mathbb{C}[x]/(p_i)$, $H^{-1}=$ dependencies, so $x^2=y^2=0$ and $x^2=y^2=x^2+y^2=0$ are distinct derived schemes.

records.title: John Rognes
records.summary: John Rognes, chromatic homotopy theory course notes. Key computation: the thick subcategory theorem (Hopkins–Smith) states every thick subcategory $T\subset \mathrm{Ho}(\mathrm{Sp}^\omega_p)$ of finite $p$-local spectra equals $\mathrm{Ho}(\mathrm{Sp}^\omega_{\ge n})$ for some $0\le n\le\infty$; Mitchell's $F(n)$ has $H^*(F(n);\mathbb{F}_p)$ free over $A(n-1)$ with $K(m)_*(F(n))=0$ for $m<n$ and $K(n)_*(F(n))\neq0$, so $\mathrm{type}(F(n))=n$, and Ravenel's result gives $\dim K(n)_*(F)\le\dim K(n+1)_*(F)$, i.e. $K(n+1)_*(F)=0\Rightarrow K(n)_*(F)=0$.

records.title: Akhil Mathew
records.summary: Akhil Mathew, perfectoid spaces course notes. Key computation: Theorem 157 (Scholze) — over the perfectoid valuation ring $V=K^\circ$ of a perfectoid field, any almost finitely generated $V$-module $M$ satisfies $M\approx V/I_{\gamma_1}\oplus V/I_{\gamma_2}\oplus\cdots$ for a unique nondecreasing sequence $\gamma_i\in\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}$ with $\gamma_i\to1$, where $I_\gamma=\{x\in V:|x|\le\gamma\}$ (or $<\gamma$), and every almost finitely generated projective module is $M\approx V^n$ for a unique $n\ge0$.

records.title: Johan Commelin
records.summary: Johan Commelin, condensed mathematics seminar: condensed abelian groups form an abelian category satisfying AB4*/AB6 with a fully faithful embedding $D^b(\mathrm{LCA})\to D(\mathrm{Cond}(\mathrm{Ab}))$ preserving Pontryagin duality. Key computation: for two completions $\mathbb{Q}_v,\mathbb{Q}_v'$ of $\mathbb{Q}$, derived solidification computes $\mathbb{Q}_v\otimes^L\mathbb{Q}_v'$; the structure theorem $0\to\mathbb{R}^n\oplus C\to A\to D\to0$ for $A\in\mathrm{LCA}$ yields $R\mathrm{Hom}(A,B)$ via the compact-open topology compatible with internal Hom, so condensed cohomology of a compact Hausdorff $S$ with $\mathbb{Z}$-coefficients equals sheaf cohomology while higher real coefficients vanish.

records.title: Neil Strickland
records.summary: Neil Strickland, recent progress in chromatic homotopy theory: reports the disproof of Ravenel's Telescope Conjecture (Burklund–Hahn–Levy–Schlank 2023). Key computation: the telescope conjecture fails for height $n>1$ while being true for $n=0,1$; equivalently $K(p,\le n)_*(X)=0$ does not force $X$ to be a filtered colimit of finite spectra $X_\alpha$ with $K(p,\le n)_*(X_\alpha)=0$.

records.title: Marius Nielsen
records.summary: Marius Nielsen, chromatic homotopy theory from the perspective of formal groups. Key computation: Quillen's theorem $L\cong MU_*$ identifies $FGL=\mathrm{Spec}(L)$ with $MU$, giving $\mathrm{Comod}_{MU_*MU}\cong\mathrm{QCoh}(M_{fg})$ and $E_2^{s,2t}=H^s(M_{fg},\omega^t)$ in the Adams spectral sequence; the thick subcategory theorem states $C\subset \mathrm{Sp}^\omega_{(p)}$ is thick iff $C$ consists of spectra of height $\le n$ for some $n$, via the height filtration $M_{fg}^{\ge n}\subset M_{fg}$ with $[p]$-multiplication factoring through $\mathrm{Frob}^n$.

records.title: C
records.summary: C. Westerland, introduction to stable homotopy theory. Key computation: the EHP fibration $S^n\to\Omega S^{n+1}\to\Omega S^{2n+1}$ with the James construction gives the split $S^{2n-1}\to\Omega\Sigma S^n$, so the EHP spectral sequence $E^1_k=\pi_k(S^{2n+1})\Rightarrow\pi_*(S^{n+1})$ computes the 2-primary stable stems; concretely the $e$-invariant element $\pi_{4n-1}(S)\otimes\mathbb{Z}\cong\mathbb{Z}_{e(n)}$ is classified by the degree of the induced map on $S^{4n-1}$.

records.title: A
records.summary: A. Mathew, stable homotopy theory course notes. Key computation: classification of the number $r(n)$ of linearly independent vector fields on $S^{n-1}$ by the Radon–Hurwitz number $\rho(n)-1$: writing $n=(2a+1)\cdot2^{4b+c}$ with $c=0,1,2,3$, then $\rho(n)=2^c+8b$, and $\beta(n)=\rho(n)-1$ independent nowhere-vanishing fields exist, equality holding up to the $J$-image; concretely $\widetilde{KO}(\mathbb{RP}^n)=\mathbb{Z}/2^c\oplus\mathbb{Z}/2^{\lceil n/2\rceil}$ computed from $KO(\mathbb{CP}^n)=\mathbb{Z}[u]/(u^{n+1})$.

records.title: Caleb Ji
records.summary: Caleb Ji, spectra and the stable homotopy category. Key computation: the homotopy groups of a spectrum $X$ are $\pi_k(X)=\mathrm{colim}_n\pi_{k+n}(X_n)$, and the smash product $X\wedge Y$ with latching structure $(X\wedge Y)_n=(X\wedge Y)_n^{\mathrm{lat}}\cup\cdots$ shows $S^0\wedge S^0=S^0$ gives $\pi_*(S)$ as the initial stable homotopy ring.

records.title: Dominic Joyce
records.summary: Dominic Joyce, derived algebraic geometry foundations and higher stacks. Key computation: for the derived zero locus $X=s^{-1}(0)$ of a section $s$ of a vector bundle $E\to V$, $L_X\simeq[E^*|_X\xrightarrow{Ds}T^*V|_X]$, perfect in degrees $[-1,0]$; explicitly $A^*=K[z_1..z_n,y_1..y_m,x_1..x_l]$ with $\deg z=0,\deg y=-1,\deg x=-2$, $dy_j=f_j(z)$, $dx_i=\sum_j g_{ij}(z)y_j$, $d^2=0$ forcing $\sum_j g_{ij}(z)f_j(z)=0$, so $H^0(A^*)=K[z]/(f_1=0,..,f_m=0)$ classifies the classical truncation $X=t_0(X)\subset\mathbb{A}^n$, with $L_X\simeq[\mathcal{O}_X^m\xrightarrow{\partial f_j/\partial z_k}\mathcal{O}_X^n]$ in degrees $[-1,0]$.

records.title: Raphaël Ponge
records.summary: Raphaël Ponge, semiclassical analysis on spectral triples extending the semiclassical Weyl law and Connes' integration formula to $p$-summable spectral triples without Hölder-regularity. Key computation: the semiclassical Weyl law $\lim_{h\to0^+}h^n N^-(h^2\Delta_g+V)=\int_M V_-(x)^{n/2}\,d\nu_g(x)$ (and $\lim h^n N^-(h^{2q}\Delta_g^q+V)=\int V_-^{n/2q}$); the main theorem — if for all $a\in A$, $a>0$, $\lim_{j\to\infty}j^{-2/p}\lambda_j(aD^2a)=\tau(a^{-p/2})$, then $\lim_{j}j^{-2/p}\lambda_j(|D|^{-q/2}a|D|^{-q/2})=\tau(a^{q/p})$ for all $q>0$, and for $V^*=V\in A$, $\lim_{h\to0^+}h^p N^-(h^2D^2+V)=\mathrm{Res}_{z=p}\,\mathrm{Tr}(V_-)^{z/2}|D|^{-z}$, recovering Connes' integration formula $\int f=\mathrm{Res}_{z=p}\mathrm{Tr}(f|D|^{-z})$.

records.title: chromatic homotopy seminar notes
records.summary: chromatic homotopy seminar notes, the nilpotence theorem and the thick subcategory theorem (Devinatz–Hopkins–Smith). Key computation: Theorem 9 (Hopkins–Smith) classifies thick subcategories of finite $p$-local spectra as exactly the $\mathcal{C}_{\ge n}=\{X:K(m)_*(X)=0\text{ for }m<n\}$; the Nilpotence theorem states $MU$ detects nilpotence ($x\in\pi_*(R)$ nilpotent iff $MU_*x$ nilpotent iff $MU_*x=0$ in $MU_*R$), so a self-map $f$ vanishing on $K(n)_0R$ forces $f$ nilpotent, and the enumeration proceeds by showing $C_{n+1}\subsetneq C_n$ is proper via Morava $K$-acyclicity.

records.title: Constantin Teleman
records.summary: Constantin Teleman, chromatic spectral sequence and stable homotopy of the spheres seminar notes: develops the $MU$-Adams (chromatic) spectral sequence $E_2=H^*(M_{fg},\omega^*)$ and computes $\pi_*L_{K(1)}S$. Key computation: for $S_1=\mathbb{G}_m(\mathbb{Z}_p^\wedge)$, $(E_1)_*=\mathbb{Z}_p^\wedge[u^{\pm1}]$; splitting $S_1=C_{p-1}\times\mathbb{Z}_p^\wedge$ ($p$ odd), $H^*(C_{p-1};\mathbb{Z}_p^\wedge[u^{\pm1}])=\mathbb{Z}_p^\wedge[u^{\pm(p-1)}]$, and $H^i(\mathbb{Z}_p^\wedge;A)=\mathbb{Z}_p^\wedge/(kp)$ for $i=2k(p-1)-1$, $k\ne0$, else $0$; the truncated chromatic spectral sequence gives the $E(q)$-local sphere agreeing with true stable stems within a finite, monotonically increasing radius (chromatic convergence), with stabilizer group $S_q\subset O_q=\mathbb{F}_{p^q}\langle S\rangle/(S^q=p,\,Sw=w^\varphi S)$ and $L_{K(n)}S\simeq E_n^{hS_n}$.

records.title: facets of spectral algebraic geometry seminar notes (KTH/SU): spectra as $S$-modules
records.summary: facets of spectral algebraic geometry seminar notes (KTH/SU): spectra as $S$-modules, $THH(A)=A\otimes^*_S A$, $TC^t$ the $S^1$-equivariant refinement, and $MP$ (the 2-periodization of $MU$) as an affine chart for the moduli stack of oriented spectral formal groups. records.title: Bhargav Bhatt
records.summary: Bhargav Bhatt, perfectoid spaces via inversions/tilting, developing the tilting correspondence and almost purity in dimension 0 and in characteristic $p$. Key computation: Theorem 3.2.8 — for a perfectoid field $K$, the tilt $L\mapsto L^\flat$ induces an equivalence of finite-étale categories $\hat{K}_{\text{ét}}\simeq \hat{K}^\flat_{\text{ét}}$, i.e. finite extensions of $K$ are classified by finite extensions of $K^\flat$; concretely $\mathbb{Z}_p^\flat\cong\mathbb{F}_p((t^{1/p^\infty}))$, with the chain $\mathrm{Perf}_K\simeq\mathrm{Perf}_{K^{\circ a}}\simeq\mathrm{Perf}_{K^{\circ a}/\pi}$ implemented by $R\mapsto R^{\circ a}$, $A\mapsto A^*/[1/t]$, $A\mapsto A/\pi$.

records.title: Krauze
records.summary: Krauze, prismatic envelopes and an explicit algorithm computing $\mathbb{Z}_p(i)(O_K/\varpi^n)$. Key computation: for $A=W(k)[[z]]$, $R=O_K/\varpi^n=A/(E(z),z^n)$, the prismatic envelope $\Delta_{R/A}=(A\{a\}/(da-r)_\delta)^\wedge_{p,d}$ is free over $R$ on monomials $\prod(\delta^u a)^{e_u}$ with $e_u<p$, and $\mathbb{Z}_p(i)(R)$ is the fiber of $\mathrm{can}-\varphi$ on the double complex over $\Delta_{R/\mathbb{Z}_p[[z_0,z_1]]}$; using the staircase bases $z^kd^c\prod f_u^{e_u}$ ($c+p^ue_u\ge i$) and a comparison lemma for differing differentials, Theorem 5.1 gives $|H^1(\mathbb{Z}_p(i)(O_K/\varpi^n))|/|H^2(\mathbb{Z}_p(i)(O_K/\varpi^n))|=q^{(n-1)i}$, hence $|K_{2i-1}(O_K/\varpi^n)|/|K_{2i-2}(O_K/\varpi^n)|=q^{(n-1)i}(q^i-1)$, and Theorem 5.2 gives even vanishing $K_{2i-2}(O_K/\varpi^n)=0$ for $i\gg0$.

records.title: Dominic Joyce
records.summary: Dominic Joyce, obstruction theories, virtual classes, and invariants: constructs virtual fundamental classes for quasi-smooth derived schemes. Key computation: for $X=s^{-1}(0)$ the derived zero locus of a section $s:V\to E$ with $V$ smooth and $E$ a vector bundle, $L_X\simeq[E^*|_X\xrightarrow{Ds}T^*V|_X]$, $\mathrm{vdim}(X)=\dim(V)-\mathrm{rank}(E)$, and $[X]^{\mathrm{virt}}=[V]\cap c_{\mathrm{rank}(E)}(E)$; for plane curves $C,D\subset\mathbb{CP}^2$ of degrees $m,n$ this gives the virtual intersection number $mn$ even when $C\cap D$ is not transverse.

records.title: Jiantong Liu
records.summary: Jiantong Liu, categorifying spectra: explains the Ramzi–Sosnilo–Winges construction showing every spectrum occurs as nonconnective $K$-theory of a small idempotent-complete stable $\infty$-category. Key computation: the Dundas–McCarthy linearization is $M\simeq\mathrm{colim}_n\Omega^n\widetilde{K}(\mathrm{Sp}^\omega;\Sigma^nM)$; identifying this colimit as $K(C_M)$ yields $K(C_M)\simeq M$ functorially, and the resulting examples show the nonconnective theorem-of-the-heart map $K(E^\heartsuit)\to K(E)$ can fail without the Noetherian hypothesis.

records.title: algebraic topology lecture notes
records.summary: algebraic topology lecture notes, an explicit Tor calculation extracting torsion. Key computation: for $R=\mathbb{Z}$ and $M=\mathbb{Z}/n$, the free resolution $0\to\mathbb{Z}\xrightarrow{n}\mathbb{Z}\to\mathbb{Z}/n\to0$ gives $\mathbb{Z}/n\otimes N\cong N/nN$ and $\mathrm{Tor}_1^{\mathbb{Z}}(\mathbb{Z}/n,N)\cong\ker(n:N\to N)$, so $\mathrm{Tor}_1$ extracts exactly the $n$-torsion of $N$.

records.title: Stefan Schwede
records.summary: Stefan Schwede, universal symmetries: global equivariant homotopy theory packages compatible equivariant homotopy theories for all compact Lie groups into global spectra and global Mackey functors. Key computation: $\pi_0^G(\mathbb{S})$ is the Burnside ring $A(G)$, freely generated by transfers $\mathrm{tr}_H^G(1)$ over conjugacy classes of closed $H\le G$ with finite Weyl group; the unit $\mathbb{S}\to KU$ sends a finite $G$-set to its permutation representation, giving the homomorphism $A(G)\to R(G)$.

records.title: Jiwu Jang
records.summary: Jiwu Jang, vertex functions of type D Nakajima quiver varieties: proves a product expression for type-$D$ vertex functions in terms of $q$-binomial factors indexed by roots. Key computation: for the $D_4$ quiver with dimension vector $v=(1,2,1,1)$ and framing $w=(0,0,0,1)$, the vertex function factors into $q$-binomial-series terms associated to specific $D_4$ roots; in the $D_1$ case $V(z)=\sum_{k\ge0}(\hbar)_k/(q)_k\cdot z^k$, the ordinary $q$-binomial series.

records.title: Vesselin Dimitrov (joint with Frank Calegari and Yunqing Tang)
records.summary: Vesselin Dimitrov (joint with Frank Calegari and Yunqing Tang), arithmetic holonomy bounds and special values of $L$-functions: proves $\mathbb{Q}$-linear independence results for $1,\zeta(2)$, and $L(2,\chi_{-3})$ using Apéry-style $G$-functions and modular periods. Key computation: with the Picard–Fuchs operator $L=x(1-x)(1-9x)d^2/dx^2+(1-20x+27x^2)d/dx+(9x-3)$, the chosen functions satisfy $L(A)=0$, $L(AB)=1$, and $L(AC)=1/(1-x)$; the Apéry limits identify $L(2,\chi_{-3})/2$ and $\zeta(2)/4$ as $w_6$-periods, producing simultaneous rational approximants.

records.title: Gabriel Dospinescu
records.summary: Gabriel Dospinescu, overview of the Fargues–Fontaine curve presenting the classification of vector bundles and its diamond-theoretic construction. Key computation: for $S=\mathrm{Spa}(C)$ geometric, every rank-$n$ vector bundle on $X_C$ is uniquely classified by a nonincreasing slope sequence $\lambda_1\ge\cdots\ge\lambda_n\in\mathbb{Q}$ through $\mathcal{E}\simeq\bigoplus_i\mathcal{O}(\lambda_i)$, equivalently by $B(\mathrm{GL}_n)$; this follows from $X_S=Y_S/\varphi^{\mathbb{Z}}$ and, for the pullback $\mathcal{F}$ to the Stein space $Y_S$, the two-term computation $R\Gamma(X_S,\mathcal{E})\simeq[\mathcal{F}(Y_S)\xrightarrow{1-\varphi}\mathcal{F}(Y_S)]$, so $H^i(X_S,\mathcal{E})=0$ for $i>1$.

records.title: Alain Connes (joint with Caterina Consani)
records.summary: Alain Connes (joint with Caterina Consani), from noncommutative geometry to tropical geometry: develops the arithmetic site and a tropical Riemann–Roch theory for the scaling quotient $C_p=\mathbb{R}_+^*/p^{\mathbb{Z}}$. Key computation: for $p>2$, principal divisors lie in the kernel of degree and the pair $(\deg,\chi)$ gives $\mathrm{Div}(C_p)/\mathcal{P}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{Z}/(p-1)\mathbb{Z}$; with $H^0(D)_\rho=\{f\in H^0(D):\lVert f\rVert_p\le\rho\}$ and $\mathrm{Dim}_{\mathbb{R}}H^0(D)=\lim_{n\to\infty}p^{-n}\dim_{\mathrm{top}}H^0(D)^{p^n}$, the slides compute $\mathrm{Dim}_{\mathbb{R}}H^0(D)-\mathrm{Dim}_{\mathbb{R}}H^0(-D)=\deg D$.

records.title: Bertrand Toën
records.summary: Bertrand Toën, derived algebraic geometry and deformation quantization: explains the canonical $(2-d)$-quantization of the derived stack $\mathrm{Bun}_G(X)$ for a compact oriented $d$-manifold (or Calabi–Yau variety). Key computation: at a $G$-bundle $E$, $T_{\mathrm{Bun}_G(X),E}\simeq C^*(X,\mathrm{ad}(E))[1]$; cup product followed by the invariant pairing on $\mathfrak{g}$ and integration over $X$ produces a nondegenerate closed 2-form of degree $2-d$, hence a $(2-d)$-shifted Poisson structure, while higher formality identifies deformations of $D_{\mathrm{qcoh}}(Z)$ as an $E_n$-monoidal dg-category with the dg Lie algebra $R\Gamma(Z,\mathrm{Sym}_{\mathcal{O}_Z}(T_Z[-1-n]))[n+1]$, yielding the quantization.

records.title: Dominic Joyce
records.summary: Dominic Joyce, triangulated categories and derived categories: culminates in the Fourier–Mukai classification of exact functors between derived categories of smooth projective schemes. Key computation: a kernel $\mathcal{E}^\bullet\in D^b\mathrm{coh}(X\times Y)$ defines $\Phi_{\mathcal{E}}(\mathcal{G}^\bullet)=R(\pi_Y)_*(L\pi_X^*\mathcal{G}^\bullet\otimes^L\mathcal{E}^\bullet)$; Mukai's formulas give its adjoints using $D_{X\times Y}(\mathcal{E}^\bullet)\otimes^L\pi_Y^*K_Y[\dim Y]$ and $D_{X\times Y}(\mathcal{E}^\bullet)\otimes^L\pi_X^*K_X[\dim X]$, and Orlov's theorem identifies every exact functor $D^b\mathrm{coh}(X)\to D^b\mathrm{coh}(Y)$ with left and right adjoints with a unique such kernel up to isomorphism.

records.title: Jonathan Wang (joint with Tony Feng)
records.summary: Jonathan Wang (joint with Tony Feng), geometric periods: categorifies the $\mathrm{GL}_2$ period formula and proves matching filtrations on its spectral and automorphic objects under geometric Langlands. Key computation: for $\check{X}=\mathrm{std}=\mathbb{A}^2$ and $X=\mathbb{G}_m\backslash\mathrm{GL}_2$, the two $\check{G}$-orbits $\{0\}$ and $\mathbb{A}^2\setminus\{0\}=\check{G}/\check{\mathrm{Mir}}_2$ yield the distinguished triangle $\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{std}}\to\Pi^{\mathrm{spec}}_*(\omega_{\mathrm{LocSys}_{\check{X}/\check{G}}})\to\mathrm{Eis}^{\mathrm{spec}}_{\check{\mathrm{Mir}}_2}(\omega_{\mathrm{LocSys}_{\mathbb{G}_m}})\xrightarrow{[1]}$, whose first term has !-stalk $\mathrm{Sym}\,H^\bullet_{\mathrm{dR}}(C,E)$; unfolding produces the matching automorphic triangle with $T_{\mathrm{Sym}(\mathrm{std})}(\mathrm{Whit})$, $\Pi_!(\mathbb{C}_{\mathrm{Bun}_X})$, and $\mathrm{Eis}_{\mathrm{Mir}_2,!}(\mathbb{C}_{\mathrm{Bun}_{\mathbb{G}_m}})$.

records.title: Sanath K
records.summary: Sanath K. Devalapurkar, equivariant homotopy theory and geometric Langlands: proves generalized derived Satake equivalences with periodic and elliptic cohomology coefficients. Key computation: for simply connected, simply laced semisimple $G$, $\mathrm{Shv}_G^c(\Omega G;KU)\otimes\mathbb{Q}\simeq\mathrm{QCoh}(\check{G}_{\mathrm{sc}}/\check{G})_{\text{2-per}}$, replacing the rational equivalence $\mathrm{Shv}_G^c(\Omega G;\mathbb{Q})\simeq\mathrm{QCoh}(\check{\mathfrak{g}}^*/\check{G})$; for an elliptic theory $A$ with curve $E$, this becomes $\mathrm{Shv}_{G/Z(G)}^c(\Omega G;A)\otimes\mathbb{Q}\simeq\mathrm{QCoh}(\mathrm{Bun}^{\mathrm{ss},0}_{\check{G}}(E))\otimes_{\pi_0A}\pi_*(A_{\mathbb{Q}})$, identifying the spectral moduli object from the coefficient theory's formal group.

records.title: Shachar Carmeli
records.summary: Shachar Carmeli, cyclotomic redshift: presents chromatic cyclotomic extensions and their height-raising behavior under algebraic $K$-theory. Key computation: the splitting $S_{T(n)}[B^nC_{p^k}]\simeq S_{T(n)}[B^nC_{p^{k-1}}]\times S_{T(n)}[\omega_{p^k}^{(n)}]$ defines a $(\mathbb{Z}/p^k)^\times$-Galois extension, and for every commutative $T(n)$-local ring spectrum $R$ the redshift equivalence $L_{T(n+1)}K(R[\omega_{p^k}^{(n)}])\simeq L_{T(n+1)}K(R)[\omega_{p^k}^{(n+1)}]$ raises its chromatic height; passing to the tower gives cyclotomic hyperdescent $L_{K(n+1)}K(R[\omega_{p^\infty}^{(n)}])^{h\mathbb{Z}}\simeq L_{K(n+1)}K(R)$.

records.title: Franz Luef
records.summary: Franz Luef, noncommutative geometry and time-frequency analysis: identifies well-localized Gabor frames with projective modules and explicit projections over noncommutative tori. Key computation: the Feichtinger module $M_s^1(\mathbb{R}^d)$ is an equivalence bimodule between $A_s^1(\alpha\mathbb{Z}\times\beta\mathbb{Z},c)$ and $A_s^1(\alpha^{-1}\mathbb{Z}\times\beta^{-1}\mathbb{Z},c)$ via the associativity identity ${}_\Lambda\langle f,g\rangle h=f\langle g,h\rangle_{\Lambda^\circ}$; a Gabor atom satisfies $p_g={}_\Lambda\langle g,g\rangle$, with $p_g^2=p_g=p_g^*$ exactly when $g\langle g,g\rangle_{\Lambda^\circ}=g$, and the canonical tight atom $h_0=S_{g,g}^{-1/2}g$ yields such a projection, existing for rectangular $\Lambda=\alpha\mathbb{Z}\times\beta\mathbb{Z}$ precisely when $\alpha\beta<1$.

records.title: Linus Hamann
records.summary: Linus Hamann, compatibility of the Fargues–Scholze and Gan–Takeda local Langlands parameters for $\mathrm{GSp}_4$ and its inner form in the stated unramified $p>2$ cases. Key computation: for a stable supercuspidal parameter $\phi$ with packets $\Pi_\phi(G)=\{\pi\}$ and $\Pi_\phi(J)=\{\rho\}$, local-shtuka cohomology is $R\Gamma_c(G,b,\mu)[\pi]\simeq\rho\otimes(\mathrm{std}\circ\phi)^\vee\otimes|\cdot|^{-3/2}[-3]$ and $R\Gamma_c(G,b,\mu)[\rho]\simeq\pi\otimes(\mathrm{std}\circ\phi)\otimes|\cdot|^{-3/2}[-3]$; for endoscopic $\mathrm{std}\circ\phi\simeq\phi_1\oplus\phi_2$, the two packet members pair with the corresponding $\phi_i$ summands.

records.title: Guozhen Wang (joint with Ruochuan Liu)
records.summary:
Guozhen Wang (joint with Ruochuan Liu), topological cyclic homology of local fields: computes the descent spectral sequences for $THH$, $TP$, and $TC$ of a local field's integers. Key computation: for $K/\mathbb{Q}_p$ with ramification index $e$ and $d=[K(\zeta_p):K]$, the slides obtain a Bott class $\beta\in E_2^{0,2d}(TC(\mathcal{O}_K);\mathbb{F}_p)$ and $E_2^{0,*}\cong\mathbb{F}_p[\beta]$, $E_2^{1,*}\cong\mathbb{F}_p[\beta]\{\lambda,\gamma\}\oplus k[\beta]\{\alpha_i^{(j)}\mid1\le i\le e,1\le j\le d\}$, $E_2^{2,*}\cong\mathbb{F}_p[\beta]\{\lambda\gamma\}$, and $E_2^{i,*}=0$ for $i\ge3$, forcing the descent spectral sequence to collapse.

Key computation: for $E=eA^q$ and $k\geq p/2$, $\operatorname{ind}D_{\nabla^E}=\frac12\operatorname{Str}(D^{-1}[D,e])^{2k+1}=\langle\operatorname{Ch}(D),\operatorname{Ch}(E)\rangle$; for $A_\theta$, $HP_0(A_\theta)=\langle\tau_0,\tau_2\rangle$ with $\tau_2(a^0,a^1,a^2)=\tau_0(a^0(\delta_1(a^1)\delta_2(a^2)-\delta_2(a^1)\delta_1(a^2)))$, giving the index pairing explicitly.

records.title: Raphaël Ponge (joint with Hang Wang)
records.summary: Raphaël Ponge (joint with Hang Wang), conformal deformation produces a twisted spectral triple whose Connes–Chern character is conformally invariant and is computed by a fixed-point local index cocycle. Key computation: $\widehat g=k^{-2}g$ gives $(C^\infty(M),L^2_{\widehat g}(M,S),D_{\widehat g})\simeq(C^\infty(M),L^2_g(M,S),\sqrt{k}D_g\sqrt{k})$ and, for the crossed product $C^\infty(M)\rtimes G$, $\sigma_g(fu_\phi)=k_\phi^{-1}fu_\phi$; for a $G$-invariant $g$, $\operatorname{Ch}(D_g)_{\sigma_g}$ is represented by $\varphi_{2m}(f^0u_{\phi_0},\ldots,f^{2m}u_{\phi_{2m}})=\frac{(-i)^{n/2}}{(2m)!}\sum_a(2\pi)^{-a/2}\int_{M_a^\phi}\widehat A(R^{TM_a^\phi})\wedge\nu_\phi(R^{N^\phi})\wedge f^0d\widehat f^1\wedge\cdots\wedge d\widehat f^{2m}$.

records.title: Nitin Nitsure
records.summary: Nitin Nitsure, cotangent-complex Ext groups classify square-zero deformation problems for schemes, morphisms, and coherent sheaves and supply Artin-style tangent–obstruction data for algebraic moduli stacks. Key computation: for a flat $f:Y\to X$ and a square-zero extension $X\hookrightarrow X'$ with ideal $I$, the transitivity triangle $f^*L_{X/X'}\to L_{Y/X'}\to L_{Y/X}\xrightarrow{[1]}$ yields $0\to\operatorname{Ext}^1(L_{Y/X},f^*I)\to\operatorname{Exal}(Y/X',f^*I)\to\operatorname{End}(f^*I)\xrightarrow{\partial}\operatorname{Ext}^2(L_{Y/X},f^*I)$; the obstruction is $\partial(\operatorname{id}_{f^*I})$, lifts form a torsor under $\operatorname{Ext}^1$, and infinitesimal automorphisms are $\operatorname{Ext}^0$.

records.summary: N. Christopher Phillips, algebraic, topological, and operator-algebraic $K$-theory share the projective-module construction, which becomes a periodic cohomology theory for Banach algebras. records.title: Xu Shen (joint with Miaofen Chen and Laurent Fargues)
records.summary: Xu Shen (joint with Miaofen Chen and Laurent Fargues), the Fargues--Rapoport conjecture classifies exactly when the admissible and weakly admissible $p$-adic period domains coincide. Key computation: a point $x\in\mathcal{F}(G,\mu)(C)$ modifies the Fargues bundle $\mathcal{E}_b$ at $\infty$ to $\mathcal{E}_{b,x}$, giving $\mathcal{F}(G,\mu,b)^a(C)=\{x\mid\mathcal{E}_{b,x}\simeq\mathcal{E}_1\}$; for basic $[b_0]\in B(G,\mu)$, one proves $\mathcal{F}(G,\mu,b_0)^a=\mathcal{F}(G,\mu,b_0)^{wa}$ iff $(G,\{\mu\})$ is fully Hodge--Newton decomposable, meaning each nonbasic $[b']\in B(G,\mu)$ has a Newton--Hodge contact point that is a break of the Newton polygon and reduces the datum to a proper Levi, with examples including $(\mathrm{GL}_h,(1,0,\ldots,0))$ and $(\mathrm{GSp}_4,(1,1,0,0))$.

records.title: Rick Jardine
records.summary: Rick Jardine, persistent homotopy admits a controlled homotopy theory in which Rips stability is preserved quantitatively by homotopy-theoretic gluing. Key computation: a finite metric sample $X$ defines the system $V_*(X):s\mapsto B P_s(X)$, and $d_H(X,Y)<r$ produces a homotopy interleaving $V_s(X)\to V_s(Y)\to V_{s+2r}(X)$, hence a $2r$-equivalence on every $\pi_n$; if a sectionwise cofibration $A\to B$ is an $r$-equivalence, every pushout $C\to B\cup_A C$ is a $2r$-equivalence, so for $X\subset Y$ and $X\subset W$ the comparison $V_*(W)\cup_{V_*(X)}V_*(Y)\to V_*(W\cup Y)$ is a $6r$-equivalence, giving a quantitative excision theorem for the Vietoris--Rips functor.

records.title: Michael Harris (joint with Wee Teck Gan and Will Sawin)
records.summary: Michael Harris (joint with Wee Teck Gan and Will Sawin), purity and globalization force ramification of Genestier--Lafforgue parameters of supercuspidal representations over local function fields. Key computation: for $F=k((t))$, a pure supercuspidal $\pi$ compactly induced from $U=G(\mathcal{O}_F)$ is globalized over $K=k(t)$ by the Poincaré series $P_\phi(g)=\sum_{\gamma\in G(K)}\phi(\gamma g)$ with $\phi_z=\phi_\pi$ for $z\in\mathbb{G}_m(k)$, $\phi_x=1_{G(\mathcal{O}_x)}$ off $|\mathbb{P}^1(k)|$, $\phi_\infty=1_{I_{\infty,+}}$, and $\phi_0=\chi_k$, whose support gives $P_\phi(1)=1$; if $L(\pi)$ were unramified, purity would extend $L(\Pi)_\sigma$ to a punctually pure tame local system on $\mathbb{G}_m$, hence a sum of finite-order tame characters, contradicting variation of $\chi_k$, so $L(\pi)$ is ramified and, for induction from a sufficiently small compact, wildly ramified.

records.title: Kęstutis Česnavičius
records.summary: Kęstutis Česnavičius, the perfectoid approach proves purity for the Brauer group and for flat cohomology with finite flat coefficients. Key computation: for a perfectoid ring $A$ and a closed $Z\subset\operatorname{Spec}(A[1/p])$ of codimension at least $2$, prismatic Dieudonné theory sends a finite locally free commutative $p$-power-order group $G$ to $M(G)=\operatorname{Ext}^1(G,\mathcal{O}_{\Prism})$ equipped with semilinear $F,V$ satisfying $FV=p$; $p$-complete arc hyperdescent reduces the resulting purity comparison to rank-one valuation rings, yielding $R\Gamma(A,G)\simeq R\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}(A[1/p])\setminus Z,G)$ and, for a regular local ring $(R,\mathfrak m)$, $H^i_{\mathfrak m}(R,G)=0$ for $i<\dim R$.

records.title: Yves André
records.summary: Yves André, every finite covering of a regular scheme is an fpqc covering, equivalently every finite extension of a regular ring is dominated by a faithfully flat algebra. Key computation: for $R=\mathbb{Z}_p[[x_2,\ldots,x_n]]$ and finite reduced $R\subset S$, adjoining all $p$-power roots gives the perfectoid algebra $R_\infty=\mathbb{Z}_p[p^{1/p^\infty}][[x_2^{1/p^\infty},\ldots,x_n^{1/p^\infty}]]^{\wedge}$; after choosing $g$ with $S[1/pg]$ étale over $R[1/pg]$, perfectoid Abhyankar makes $S_\infty^\infty$ $(pg)^{1/p^\infty}$-almost finite étale over $R_\infty^\infty$, and $T=\Sigma^{-1}(\prod_{\mathbb N}S_\infty^\infty/\bigoplus_{\mathbb N}S_\infty^\infty)$ removes almostness to produce a perfectoid $S$-algebra faithfully flat over $R$.

records.title: Jessica Fintzen
records.summary: Jessica Fintzen, explicitly constructed omni-supercuspidal types force arbitrary algebraic automorphic forms to be congruent modulo $p^m$ to forms supercuspidal at $p$. Key computation: when $p$ exceeds the Coxeter number of $G$, there are nested compact opens $U_{p,1}\supset U_{p,2}\supset\cdots$ and maps $\lambda_m:U_{p,m}\twoheadrightarrow\mathbb{Z}/p^m\mathbb{Z}$ such that $(U_{p,m},\psi\circ\lambda_m)$ is a supercuspidal type for every nontrivial $\psi$; consequently $M(U_{p,m}U^p,\mathbb{Z}_p)/p^m\simeq M(U_{p,m}U^p,A_m)$ Hecke-equivariantly, and every automorphic representation contributing to $M(U_{p,m}U^p,A_m)\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}_p}\mathbb{Q}_p$ has supercuspidal local factor at $p$.

records.title: David Vogan
records.summary: David Vogan, real parabolic induction, cohomological induction, and weakly unipotent representations reduce the construction of large portions of the unitary dual to unitary data on Levi subgroups. Key computation: for a $\theta$-stable $P=LU$ and an $(\mathfrak l,L\cap K)$-module $\pi_L$ of infinitesimal character $\gamma=\gamma_z+\gamma_d$, Zuckerman's functors satisfy $R^i(\pi_L)=0$ for $i<s$ and $R^s(\pi_L)$ is unitary when $\pi_L$ is weakly unipotent unitary and $\gamma_z$ is weakly antidominant on coroots of $U$; for $G=\mathrm{GL}(2n)$, $L=\mathrm{GL}(n)\times\mathrm{GL}(n)$, and $\pi_L=(1\otimes|\det|^a)\otimes(1\otimes|\det|^b)$, one has $\gamma_z=[(a,\ldots,a)(b,\ldots,b)]$ and the required central condition is exactly $a-b\ge0$.

records.title: Mark Goresky (with Robert MacPherson
records.summary: Mark Goresky (with Robert MacPherson, Günter Harder, and Robert Kottwitz), weighted cohomology turns Arthur's topological trace formula into a Lefschetz fixed-point formula for Hecke correspondences on arithmetic locally symmetric spaces. Key computation: the middle-weight truncation on the reductive Borel--Serre compactification satisfies $R\pi_*W^\mu H^*(X^{\mathrm{RBS}})\simeq IH^*(X^{\mathrm{BB}})\simeq H_{(2)}^*(X)$; for a hyperbolic fixed component $F$, its local term is $\operatorname{lc}(F)=\sum_i(-1)^i\operatorname{Tr}(C^*\mid H^i_{\{\mathrm{expanding}\}}(U,A^\bullet))$, and summing these boundary-stratum contributions recovers Arthur's $L^2$ Lefschetz number $L(C(h))=\sum_i(-1)^i\operatorname{Tr}(q_*p^*\mid H^i_{(2)}(X;E_\rho))$ and the discrete-series character factor.

records.title: Guozhen Wang (joint with Ruochuan Liu)
records.summary: Guozhen Wang (joint with Ruochuan Liu), prismatic descent computes the mod-$p$ topological cyclic homology of $\mathbb{Z}_p$ from a perfectoid resolution. Key computation: for $R=\mathbb{Z}_p[p^{1/p^\infty}]^{\wedge}$, the descent Hopf algebroid gives $E_2^{*,*,*}=\mathbb{F}_p[f,g,\sigma^{\pm1}]/(g^2)$, and with $\psi(k)=(p^k-1)/(p-1)$ its Tate differentials are $d_{p\psi(k)}(f^{p^{k-1}})=g f^{p^{k-1}+\psi(k)-1}$; the survivors recover $(\mathrm{TC}/p)_*(\mathbb{Z}_p)$ as a free $\mathbb{F}_p[v_1]$-module on $\{1,\gamma,a_0\gamma,a_m\mid0\le m\le p-1\}$, in stems $0,-1,2p-2$, and $2p-2m-1$ respectively.

records.title: Neil Strickland
records.summary: Neil Strickland, Morava $K$-theories classify the thick subcategories of finite spectra and organize stable homotopy into chromatic layers. Key computation: a finite $p$-local spectrum $X$ has type $n$ when $K(p,n)_*(X)\ne0$ but $K(p,m)_*(X)=0$ for $m<n$, defining $\mathcal{F}(p,n)$; every thick subcategory is one of the $\mathcal{F}(p,n)$, while periodicity supplies $v:\Sigma^dX\to X$ inducing an isomorphism on $K(p,n)_*(X)$, and chromatic convergence decomposes $\pi_*X$ into layers controlled by $K(p,n)$ with eventual periods $2(p^n-1)p^k$.

records.title: Gautier Ponsinet
records.summary: Gautier Ponsinet, universal norms of de Rham representations over perfectoid extensions are controlled by the positive Hodge--Tate part via the Fargues--Fontaine curve. Key computation: if $V$ is de Rham with Hodge--Tate weights at most $1$ and $V_0\subset V$ is minimal such that $V/V_0$ has weights at most $0$, then for $T_0=T\cap V_0$ and perfectoid $\widehat L$, $H_e^1(L,V/T)=\operatorname{Im}(H^1(L,V_0/T_0)\to H^1(L,V/T))$; for an abelian variety, $\widetilde{\widehat A}=\varprojlim_{[p]}\widehat A\simeq\Gamma(X_{FF},\mathcal{E}(\widetilde{\widehat A}))$ with all Harder--Narasimhan slopes positive, so the bundle classification gives $H^1(L,\widetilde{\widehat A})=0$ and recovers the Coates--Greenberg description of the Kummer image.

records.title: Christian Sattler and David Wärn
records.summary: Christian Sattler and David Wärn, a short proposition-valued axiom system inside homotopy type theory reconstructs the basic calculus of univalent $\infty$-categories. Key computation: defining $[0]=\mathbf{1}$ and $[n+1]=\operatorname{Fun}([n],I)$, the Segal pushout $[2]\simeq I\amalg_{\mathbf{1}}I$ makes $\operatorname{Map}([2],C)\simeq\operatorname{Map}(I,C)\times_{\operatorname{Ob}(C)}\operatorname{Map}(I,C)$ and hence defines composition; inductively $[n]$ is the colimit of its spine, giving $\operatorname{Map}([n],C)\simeq\sum_{a:\operatorname{Fin}(n+1)\to\operatorname{Ob}(C)}\prod_{i:\operatorname{Fin}(n)}C(a_i,a_{i+1})$, while the Rezk axiom identifies $(x\simeq y)\simeq(x=y)$.

records.title: Gabriele Vezzosi
records.summary: Gabriele Vezzosi, derived algebraic geometry realizes the reduced obstruction theory for stable maps to a K3 surface as the cotangent complex of a quasi-smooth derived Deligne--Mumford stack. Key computation: for a stable map $f:C\to S$, the standard obstruction space fits into $H^1(C,T_C)\to H^1(C,f^*T_S)\to\operatorname{Obs}_f\to0$, and the symplectic identification $T_S\simeq\Omega_S^1$ followed by $df$ gives a surjection $a:\operatorname{Obs}_f\to H^1(C,\omega_C)\simeq\mathbb{C}$, forcing $[\overline{M}_g(S;\beta)]_{\mathrm{std}}^{\mathrm{vir}}=0$; removing this factor produces a quasi-smooth $R\overline{M}_g^{\mathrm{red}}(S;\beta)$ with obstruction space $\ker a$ and the nontrivial reduced virtual class.

records.title: Jared Weinstein
records.summary: Jared Weinstein, diamonds turn analytic adic spaces over $\mathbb{Z}_p$ into pro-étale sheaves and identify perfectoid spaces over $\mathbb{Q}_p$ with characteristic-$p$ perfectoid spaces over the diamond $\operatorname{Spd}\mathbb{Q}_p$. Key computation: $\operatorname{Spd}\mathbb{Q}_p=(\operatorname{Spd}\mathbb{Q}_p^{\mathrm{cycl}})/\mathbb{Z}_p^*$ and $(\operatorname{Spd}\mathbb{Q}_p)(S)=\{S^\sharp\to\operatorname{Spa}\mathbb{Q}_p:(S^\sharp)^\flat\simeq S\}$; for $R$ a $\mathbb{Q}_p$-vector space the associated diamond $\widetilde H_C^\diamond(R)=H^0(X_{R^\flat},\mathcal O(1))$ fits into $0\to\mathbb{Q}_p(1)\to\widetilde H_C^\diamond\to\mathbb A_C^{1,\diamond}\to0$, and the construction yields $\{\text{perfectoid spaces}/\mathbb{Q}_p\}\simeq\{X/\mathbb F_p\text{ perfectoid}:X\to\operatorname{Spd}\mathbb{Q}_p\}$.

records.title: Charles Rezk
records.summary: Charles Rezk, height-$2$ Morava $E$-theory at $p=2$ gives an explicit twisted bialgebra of power operations, making $\pi_0$ of every $K(2)$-local commutative $E$-algebra an amplified $\Gamma$-ring. Key computation: for $E_0=\mathbb Z_2[[a]]$, additive operations $Q_0,Q_1,Q_2$ satisfy $Q_1Q_0=2Q_2Q_1-2Q_0Q_2$, $Q_2Q_0=Q_0Q_1+aQ_0Q_2-2Q_1Q_2$, and $Q_0(x)=x^2+2\theta(x)$; their Cartan formulas are encoded by $\Delta(Q_0)=Q_0\otimes Q_0+2Q_1\otimes Q_2+2Q_2\otimes Q_1$ and analogous displayed formulas for $\Delta(Q_1),\Delta(Q_2)$, while $\Gamma$ has left $\mathbb Z_2[[a]]$-basis $Q_0^iQ_{j_1}\cdots Q_{j_r}$ with $j_k\in\{1,2\}$, yielding $\pi_0L_{K(2)}\mathbb P_E(E)\simeq \widehat F_{(2,a)}$ for the free amplified $\Gamma$-ring $F$.

records.title: Agnès Beaudry
records.summary: Agnès Beaudry, the extended Morava stabilizer group realizes the $K(n)$-local sphere as homotopy fixed points of Morava $E$-theory and turns the local Adams--Novikov spectral sequence into continuous group cohomology. Key computation: Lubin--Tate deformation theory gives $(E_n)_0=\mathbb Z_{p^n}[[u_1,\ldots,u_{n-1}]]$ representing deformations of the height-$n$ Honda formal group and $\mathbb G_n=\{(f,i):i\in\operatorname{Gal}(\mathbb F_{p^n}/\mathbb F_p),\ f:i^*\Gamma_n\xrightarrow\sim\Gamma_n\}$; Goerss--Hopkins--Miller lifts its action to $E_n$, and $(E_n)_*E_n\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_c(\mathbb G_n,(E_n)_*)$ promotes to $L_{K(n)}E_n^{\bullet+1}\simeq F_c((\mathbb G_n)^{\bullet+},E_n)$, hence $L_{K(n)}S^0\simeq E_n^{h\mathbb G_n}$ with $H_c^*(\mathbb G_n,(E_n)_*)\Longrightarrow\pi_*L_{K(n)}S^0$.

records.title: Dominic Joyce
records.summary: Dominic Joyce, Koszul cdgas retain relations among defining equations and make derived intersections quasi-smooth with the expected virtual dimension, recovering Bézout counts without transversality. Key computation: for $p_1,\ldots,p_n\in\mathbb C[x_1,\ldots,x_m]$, the cdga $A^*=\mathbb C[x_1,\ldots,x_m;y_1,\ldots,y_n]$ with $|y_i|=-1$ and $dy_i=p_i$ has $H^0(A^*)=\mathbb C[x_1,\ldots,x_m]/(p_1,\ldots,p_n)$ but its $H^{-1}$ distinguishes dependent presentations such as $(x^2,y^2)$ and $(x^2,y^2,x^2+y^2)$; thus $\operatorname{Spec}A^*$ has $\operatorname{vdim}=m-n$, and for plane curves $C,D\subset\mathbb{CP}^2$ of degrees $m,n$, the derived intersection $C\times^R_{\mathbb{CP}^2}D$ is proper quasi-smooth of virtual dimension $0$ with $[C\times^R_{\mathbb{CP}^2}D]^{\mathrm{virt}}=mn$ even when the classical intersection has dimension $1$.

records.title: Giovanni Landi
records.summary: Giovanni Landi, Connes's reconstruction theorem characterizes compact oriented spin$^c$ manifolds spectrally, with the Dirac operator recovering dimension, distance, and measure from the commutative algebra. Key computation: an $n$-dimensional spectral triple has resolvent singular values $\mu_k(|D|)\sim2\pi\bigl(k/(\Omega_n\operatorname{vol}M)\bigr)^{1/n}$ and Connes's distance formula $d(p,q)=\sup\{|f(p)-f(q)|:f\in C^\infty(M),\ \|[D,f]\|\le1\}$, while integration is the Dixmier trace $\int_M f\,d\mu_g\sim\mathop{\rlap{-}\!\int}f|D|^{-n}$; imposing the first-order and orientability relations together with the spectral conditions and multiplicity $2^{n/2}$ reconstructs $A=C^\infty(M)$ and $D$ as a Dirac operator, whereas the noncommutative example $(A(SU_q(2)),H,D)$ is regular, $3^+$-summable, and has dimension spectrum $\{1,2,3\}$ and $KO$-dimension $3$.

records.title: Matthew Kennedy (joint results with Eli Shamovich and with Laurent Marcoux and Mikael…
records.summary: Matthew Kennedy (joint results with Eli Shamovich and with Laurent Marcoux and Mikael Rørdam Skoufranis), noncommutative Choquet theory classifies matrix-convex simplices and turns majorization of operator tuples into existence of a doubly stochastic completely positive map. Key computation: a compact noncommutative convex set $K$ is an nc simplex precisely when each $x\in K$ has a unique maximal representing nc state, equivalently $A(K)^{**}$ is a von Neumann algebra; the nc Choquet order is the dilation order $\mu\prec_{\mathrm{nc}}\nu$ iff a Stinespring representation satisfies $\pi_\nu|_{A(K)}=\begin{psmallmatrix}\pi_\mu|_{A(K)}&*\\ *&*\end{psmallmatrix}$. Consequently, for self-adjoint tuples $a=(a_i),b=(b_i)$ in a finite von Neumann algebra $(M,\tau)$, the inequalities $f(a)\le f(b)$ for every continuous convex nc function $f$ are equivalent to $a_i=\varphi(b_i)$ for all $i$ under one normal unital completely positive trace-preserving map $\varphi:M\to M$.

records.title: Jamie Mingo
records.summary: Jamie Mingo, noncrossing-partition cumulants characterize free independence and convert the moment sequence of a noncommutative random variable into Voiculescu's compositional-transform equation. Key computation: Möbius inversion on $NC(n)$ gives $\kappa_n(a_1,\ldots,a_n)=\sum_{\pi\in NC(n)}\mu_{NC(n)}(\pi,1_n)\varphi_\pi(a_1,\ldots,a_n)$ and $\varphi(a_1\cdots a_n)=\sum_{\pi\in NC(n)}\kappa_\pi(a_1,\ldots,a_n)$; unital subalgebras $A_1,\ldots,A_s$ are freely independent iff every mixed cumulant vanishes, namely $\kappa_n(a_1,\ldots,a_n)=0$ whenever $a_i\in A_{j_i}$ and $\ker(j)\ne1_n$. Decomposing a noncrossing partition by the block containing $1$ yields $m_n=\sum_{s=1}^n\kappa_s\sum_{i_1+\cdots+i_s+s=n}m_{i_1}\cdots m_{i_s}$, hence $C(zM(z))=M(z)$ and $R(z)=G^{\langle-1\rangle}(z)-z^{-1}$.

records.summary: Andrew J. Blumberg, trace methods identify topological Hochschild homology by the Hill--Hopkins--Ravenel norm and recover $TR$ and $TC$ from curves in algebraic $K$-theory. records.title: Maria Yakerson
records.summary: Maria Yakerson, finite-flat transfers give a universal framed model for connective motivic algebraic $K$-theory and a Hilbert-scheme presentation over a perfect field. records.title: Emily Riehl
records.summary: Emily Riehl, univalent foundations encode higher-categorical composition by contractibility and support a machine computation of $\pi_4(S^3)$. Key computation: univalence makes $\operatorname{id\text{-}to\text{-}equiv}:(A=_{\mathcal U}B)\to(A\simeq B)$ an equivalence, while the composite space $\operatorname{Comp}(f,g)$ of two paths is a pullback of $\operatorname{Map}(\Delta,X)\to\operatorname{Map}(\Lambda,X)$ and is contractible because $D^n\times\Delta$ deformation-retracts onto $S^{n-1}\times\Delta\cup_{S^{n-1}\times\Lambda}D^n\times\Lambda$; this contractible-choice principle supplies composition in synthetic $\infty$-categories, and the constructive Hopf-fibration/Freudenthal/Blakers--Massey calculation normalizes in Cubical Agda to the Brunerie number $n=-2$, hence $\pi_4(S^3)\cong\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$.

records.summary: Pádraig Daly, operator-system methods classify quantum superchannels, prove every channel-space supermap extends to a superchannel, and characterize extreme constrained completely positive extensions. Key computation: the Choi map identifies $S_{\mathrm{CPTP}}(d,r)$ completely order isomorphically with $S(d,r)=\{(P_{ij}):\operatorname{Tr}P_{ii}=\operatorname{Tr}P_{jj},\ \operatorname{Tr}P_{ij}=0\ (i\ne j)\}$; a CPTP-preserving $\Gamma$ is a quantum superchannel exactly when the induced $\widetilde\Gamma:S(d_1,r_1)\to S(d_2,r_2)$ is completely positive, so Arveson's extension theorem and Choi's theorem produce $S(\varphi)=\psi_{\mathrm{post}}\circ(\operatorname{id}_e\otimes\varphi)\circ\psi_{\mathrm{pre}}$, with minimal $e=\operatorname{rank}(\operatorname{Tr}_{r_1}\operatorname{Tr}_{r_2}C_{\widetilde S})$; two extensions induce the same action precisely subject to $\operatorname{Tr}_{d_1}(C_{\widetilde S_1}-C_{\widetilde S_2})=0$.

records.title: Reyer Sjamaar (joint work with Florian Dorsch
records.summary: Reyer Sjamaar (joint work with Florian Dorsch, Miguel Cueca, and Chenchang Zhu), derived higher Lie groupoids encode singular symplectic reduction as a shifted symplectic groupoid Morita equivalent to a derived Lagrangian intersection. Key computation: a derived manifold $\mathcal M=(M,E_\bullet,X_\bullet)$ has tangent complex $T_mM\to E_{1,m}\to\cdots$, and weak equivalences are bijective on classical loci and quasi-isomorphisms on these complexes; for a Hamiltonian $G$-manifold $(M,\omega,\mu)$, the derived action groupoid $G\times(\mathfrak g^*\times M)\rightrightarrows(\mathfrak g^*\times M)$ has tangent total complex $0\to\mathfrak g\to T_mM\to\mathfrak g^*\to0$, while $(\omega,\mu)$ is closed in the de Rham triple complex because $d\omega=0$ and $\delta\omega=d\mu$, and its induced pairing is a quasi-isomorphism $T\simeq T^\vee$, giving the $0$-shifted symplectic derived quotient $M//G$.

records.title: Adam Humeniuk
records.summary: Adam Humeniuk, the $C^*$-covers of a nonselfadjoint operator algebra form a complete lattice, and explicit constructions separate five natural notions of equality of cover data. Key computation: ordering covers by $(C,\iota)\geq(D,\eta)$ when a surjective $*$-homomorphism $C\twoheadrightarrow D$ intertwines $\iota$ and $\eta$ makes $C^*\!\operatorname{-Lat}(A)$ a complete lattice with extrema $C^*_{\max}(A)$ and $C^*_{\mathrm{env}}(A)$; the formulas $C^*\!\operatorname{-Lat}(A\oplus B)\cong C^*\!\operatorname{-Lat}(A)\times C^*\!\operatorname{-Lat}(B)$ and, for nuclear simple $B$, $C^*\!\operatorname{-Lat}(A\otimes B)\cong C^*\!\operatorname{-Lat}(A)\otimes B$ yield examples such as $T_2$ and $T_2\otimes M_2\cong M_2(T_2)$ that are lattice-isomorphic but not lattice-intertwined, proving that isomorphism, intertwining, lattice $*$-isomorphism, lattice isomorphism, and cover equivalence are genuinely distinct.

records.summary: Michael Brannan (joint with Kari Eifler, Christian Voigt, and Moritz Weber), quantum graphs admit universal quantum Cuntz--Krieger algebras that recover the classical construction for commutative vertex algebras and exhibit new nonnuclear examples. Key computation: for $\mathcal G=(B,\psi,A)$ with $B=\bigoplus_{k=1}^mM_{n(k)}(\mathbb C)$, writing $S^{(k)}=(\dim B/n(k))[S(e_{ij}^{(k)})]$ turns the defining relation $\mu(1\otimes\mu)(S\otimes S^*\otimes S)(1\otimes m^*)m^*=S$ into $S^{(k)}S^{(k)*}S^{(k)}=S^{(k)}$, while $\mu(S^*\otimes S)m^*=\mu(S\otimes S^*)m^*A$ becomes $S^{(k)*}S^{(k)}=(S^{(1)}S^{(1)*},\ldots,S^{(m)}S^{(m)*})\widetilde A$; these relations define $\mathcal O_{\mathcal G}$, give $\mathcal O_{\mathcal G}$ equal to the usual Cuntz--Krieger algebra when $B$ is abelian, and for the complete quantum graph yield the explicit quotient $\mathcal O_{K(M_n)}\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal O_{n^2}$ by $S_{ij}\mapsto n^{-1/2}\widehat S_{ij}$.

records.title: Dominic Joyce
records.summary: Dominic Joyce, global quotient stacks form a $(2,1)$-category in which classifying stacks retain automorphisms of principal bundles and $2$-fibre products differ essentially from fibre products in the homotopy category. records.title: Dominic Joyce
records.summary: Dominic Joyce, Dwyer--Kan hammock localization upgrades inversion of weak equivalences from an ordinary homotopy category to a simplicial model for the associated $\infty$-category, while horn filling distinguishes categories, groupoids, and quasicategories. Key computation: for a model category $\mathcal M$, the mapping simplicial set $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{DK}}(X,Y)$ is built from rows of zigzags $X\leftarrow^{\sim}K_1\leftarrow^{\sim}L_1\to K_2\leftarrow^{\sim}\cdots\to Y$, and $\pi_0\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{DK}}(X,Y)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal M[W^{-1}]}(X,Y)$; moreover a simplicial set is $N(\mathcal C)$ exactly when every inner horn has a unique filler, and $N(\mathcal C)$ is Kan exactly when $\mathcal C$ is a groupoid, identifying Kan complexes as models for $\infty$-groupoids and weak Kan complexes as quasicategories.

records.summary: Yiannis Sakellaridis (joint with Chen Wan), comparison of the Jacquet--Zagier and Kuznetsov trace formulas separates the residual spectrum of $\mathrm{GL}_n$ into boundary terms indexed by generic length. Key computation: after partially compactifying Whittaker test functions there is an isomorphism $U:\mathcal S(G/G)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal S^+((N,\psi)\backslash G/(N,\psi))$ pulling stable characters back to relative characters and satisfying $\mathrm{STF}(f)=\mathrm{KTF}(Uf)+\sum_{j=1}^{n-1}B_j(f)$; the Kuznetsov main term has spectral expansion over generic automorphic representations, whereas $B_j$ has expansion over representations of generic length $n-j$, and meromorphic comparison in a parameter $s$ pairs the divergence of the naive trace formula with the pole of $L(\pi,\operatorname{Ad},s)$, so taking $\operatorname{Res}_{s=1}$ yields the noninvariant trace-formula identity with all residual boundary contributions separated.

records.title: Bill Casselman
records.summary: Bill Casselman, the inverse Satake transform gives an explicit basic Schwartz function for every irreducible finite-dimensional representation of $\widehat{\mathrm{GL}}_2$, reducing the construction to symmetric-power multiplicities and vector partition functions. records.summary: Malors Espinosa (joint with Melissa Emory, Debanjana Kundu, and Tian An Wong), interpolation and Poisson summation isolate the trivial and special-representation traces inside the regular elliptic trace formula for $\mathrm{GL}_2$ over a totally real number field. Key computation: contributing elliptic classes are exactly $(\tau,u)\in\mathcal O_K\times\mathcal O_K^\times$ with $\tau^2-4u\epsilon$ nonsquare, and $(\tau^2-4u\epsilon)=\mathfrak S_\gamma^2\Delta_\gamma$ defines $O(z,\gamma)=N(\mathfrak S_\gamma)^z\sum_{\mathfrak d\mid\mathfrak S_\gamma}N(\mathfrak d)^{1-2z}\prod_{\mathfrak q\mid\mathfrak d'}(1-\chi_\gamma(\mathfrak q)N(\mathfrak q)^{-z})$; then $O(1,\gamma)=\prod_{\mathfrak q}O(\gamma,f_\mathfrak q)$ and $\Lambda(z,\chi_\gamma)O(z,\gamma)=\Lambda(1-z,\chi_\gamma)O(1-z,\gamma)$, while Poisson summation gives $\operatorname{Tr}(1(f))=p^{-k/2}(1-p^{-(k+1)})(1-p^{-1})^{-1}\sum_\pm\int_{\mathbb R^{2n-1}}\theta_\pm(x,y)\,dx\,dy$ and identifies the second residue as $-2$ times the special-representation trace.

records.summary: Joachim Zacharias (joint with Joan Bosa, Francesc Perera, and Jianchao Wu), almost elementary actions have $\mathcal Z$-stable crossed products and unify almost finite dynamics with $\mathcal Z$-stability of simple nuclear algebras. Key computation: a noncommutative tower is a c.p.c. order-zero map $\lambda:M_n\otimes C(S)\to A$ satisfying $\lambda(\,\cdot\,\otimes\delta_g)=\alpha_{gh^{-1}}\lambda(\,\cdot\,\otimes\delta_h)$; castles approximating finite sets with $1-\lambda(h)\precsim_G b$ and $\|h-g\cdot h\|<\varepsilon$ define almost elementariness, for which $\alpha:G\curvearrowright A\Rightarrow A\rtimes_\alpha G$ is almost elementary and hence $\mathcal Z$-stable, while for $A=C(X)$ and amenable $G$ the condition is equivalent to almost finiteness of $G\curvearrowright X$.

Sehnem (joint with Zahra Afsar, Marcelo Laca, and Jacqui Ramagge), the KMS$_\beta$ simplex of a Toeplitz noncommutative torus is classified by probability measures on a torus determined by the degeneracy of its zero-energy block. Key computation: for $r=(r_1,\ldots,r_k,0_d)$, every KMS state satisfies $\varphi(L_pL_xL_y^*L_q^*)=\delta_{p,q}e^{-\beta\langle p,r\rangle}\varphi(L_xL_y^*)$ and is obtained from a trace $\omega$ on $Q\mathcal T_r(\mathbb N^n,\sigma_\Theta)Q$ by $T_\beta(\omega)(X)=Z(\beta)^{-1}\sum_{l\in\mathbb N^k\times0_d}e^{-\beta\langle l,r\rangle}\omega(QL_l^*XL_lQ)$, where $Q=\prod_{j=1}^k(1-L_{e_j}L_{e_j}^*)$ and $Z(\beta)=\sum_pe^{-\beta\langle p,r\rangle}$; since traces on $A_{\Theta_d}$ are states on $Z(A_{\Theta_d})\cong C(\mathbb T^m)$, this gives $\operatorname{KMS}_\beta\cong\mathcal M_1(\mathbb T^m)$.

records.title: Sarah Reznikoff (joint with Jonathan Brown
records.summary: Sarah Reznikoff (joint with Jonathan Brown, Adam Fuller, and David Pitts), regular ideals of a $C^*$-algebra are classified by invariant regular ideals of a regular subalgebra, and regular graph-algebra quotients preserve Condition (L). Key computation: for a regular inclusion $B\subseteq A$ with faithful invariant expectation $E:A\to B$ and regular ideal intersection property, $J\mapsto J\cap B$ and $K\mapsto J_K=\{a\in A:E(a^*a)\in K^{\perp\perp}\}$ are inverse Boolean-algebra isomorphisms between regular ideals of $A$ and invariant regular ideals of $B$; for graph algebras, $J=J^{\perp\perp}$ is equivalent to $p_w\in J\Longleftrightarrow(\forall v\in T(w))(\exists u\in T(v))\,p_u\in H(J)$, which forces every cycle of $E/J$ to retain an entrance and hence preserves Condition (L).
