records.title: Paul Skoufranis
records.summary: Paul Skoufranis, tracial inequalities completely characterize convex hulls of unitary orbits of self-adjoint elements in arbitrary unital $C^*$-algebras and extend to joint majorization of commuting tuples. Key computation: for self-adjoint $S,T\in A$, one has $S\in\overline{\operatorname{conv}}(\mathcal U(T))$ exactly when $\tau((S-\alpha)_+)\le\tau((T-\alpha)_+)$ and $\tau((-S-\alpha)_+)\le\tau((-T-\alpha)_+)$ for every lower-semicontinuous trace $\tau$ and $\alpha\in\mathbb R$; in $M_n$, this is equivalent to $\sum_{k=1}^ma_k\le\sum_{k=1}^mb_k$ for ordered eigenvalues (equality at $m=n$), to $a=Xb$ for a doubly stochastic $X$, and to a unital trace-preserving completely positive map $\Psi$ with $\Psi(T)=S$.

records.title: Dan Ursu (joint with Shirly Geffen)
records.summary: Dan Ursu (joint with Shirly Geffen), simplicity of reduced crossed products by FC-hypercentral groups is characterized by the absence of a central corner on which a finite-conjugacy element acts inner with centralizer-invariant implementer. Key computation: for a minimal action $\alpha:G\curvearrowright A$ with $G$ FC-hypercentral, $A\rtimes_rG$ is not simple exactly when there exist $t\in\mathrm{FC}(G)\setminus\{e\}$, a nonzero $t$-invariant $p\in Z(I(A))$, and $u\in\mathcal U(I(A)p)$ such that $\alpha_t|_{I(A)p}=\operatorname{Ad}(u)$ and $\alpha_s(p)=p,\ \alpha_s(u)=u$ for every $s\in C_G(t)$; this refines proper outerness on the injective envelope and is equivalent, for separable $A$, to an intrinsic obstruction on an essential $t$-invariant ideal $J\triangleleft A$ with an implementing unitary in $M(J)$.

records.title: Matthew Kennedy
records.summary: Matthew Kennedy, noncommutative Choquet theory classifies operator systems by compact matrix-convex state spaces and characterizes those arising from $C^*$-algebras as noncommutative Bauer simplices. Key computation: matrix convexity closes $K=\coprod_nK_n$ under $\sum_i\alpha_i^*x_i\alpha_i$ whenever $\sum_i\alpha_i^*\alpha_i=I$, and evaluation gives the dual equivalence $S\cong A(K)$; every $x\in K_n$ has a maximal representing nc state $\mu:C(K)\to M_n$ with $a(x)=\int_Ka\,d\lambda$ supported on $\partial K$, while uniqueness of this maximal state is equivalent to $A(K)^{**}$ being a von Neumann algebra and to $A(K)\otimes_cT=A(K)\otimes_{\max}T$ for every operator system $T$; adding closed $\partial K$ characterizes precisely nc state spaces of unital $C^*$-algebras.

records.title: Kenneth R
records.summary: Kenneth R. Davidson, free semigroup algebras admit a Lebesgue--von Neumann--Wold decomposition and are uniformly hyperreflexive. Key computation: on Fock space $\mathcal F_n^2=\ell^2(\mathbb F_n^+)$ the left shifts satisfy $L_i^*L_j=\delta_{ij}I$ and $\sum_iL_iL_i^*=I-\xi_\varnothing\xi_\varnothing^*$, while $\mathcal L_n'=\mathcal R_n$ and every $A\in\mathcal L_n$ has Ces\`aro-summed Fourier expansion $A\sim\sum_wa_wL_w$; the structure projection $P$ determined by $\bigcap_{k\ge1}\mathcal S_0^k=\mathcal WP$ splits an arbitrary free semigroup algebra into von Neumann and type-$L$ corners, and Kennedy's wandering-vector theorem for absolutely continuous representations yields $\mathcal S\simeq\mathcal L^{(\alpha)}\oplus\mathcal S_a\oplus\mathcal S_{vN}\oplus\mathcal S_d$, with every free semigroup algebra hyperreflexive with constant at most $6$.

records.title: Michael Brannan
records.summary: Michael Brannan, complete quantum graphs have no finite classical coloring but have quantum chromatic number exactly $n^2$, and their coloring algebras possess strongly solid noninjective factor representations. Key computation: the algebra $\mathcal A(\operatorname{Hom}(QK_n,K_{n^2}))$ is generated by $p_{ij}^{(a)}$ with $p_{ij}^{(a)}p_{kl}^{(a)}=\delta_{jk}n^{-1}p_{il}^{(a)}$, $\sum_jp_{ij}^{(a)}p_{jk}^{(b)}=\delta_{ab}p_{ik}^{(a)}$, $\sum_ip_{ii}^{(a)}=n^{-1}1$, and $\sum_ap_{ij}^{(a)}=\delta_{ij}1$; any unitary error basis $\{u_a\}_{a=1}^{n^2}\subset U(M_n)$ gives the representation $p_{ij}^{(a)}\mapsto n^{-1}u_a^*e_{ij}u_a$, while the quantum Hoffman bound supplies the reverse inequality, proving $\chi_q(QK_n)=n^2$ whereas $\chi_{\mathrm{loc}}(QK_n)=\infty$; for $n\ge3$ the same universal algebra has a faithful trace whose GNS algebra is a strongly solid noninjective $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor.

records.title: Ra\'ul E
records.summary: Ra\'ul E. Curto (joint with In Sung Hwang and Woo Young Lee), Potapov's factorization theorem extends from matrices to rational two-sided inner operator-valued functions. Key computation: rationality is defined by the Hankel-kernel condition $\theta H^2(\mathbb T,E)\subseteq\ker H_{\Phi^*}$ for a finite Blaschke product $\theta$; if an inner $\Delta$ divides $\Theta=\theta I_E$, then $\Delta$ is a finite product of Blaschke--Potapov factors $b_\alpha P_M+(I_E-P_M)$, and the Beurling--Lax--Halmos identity $\ker H_{\Phi^*}=\Delta H^2$ yields the coprime factorization $\Phi=\Delta A^*$; consequently a two-sided inner $\Phi\in H^\infty(\mathbb T,B(E))$ is rational exactly when it is a finite Blaschke--Potapov product.

records.title: Ryan O'Loughlin
records.summary: Ryan O'Loughlin, compact truncated Toeplitz operators on a model space have continuous inner-multiple symbols exactly under the same conditions that give bounded symbols for all bounded truncated Toeplitz operators. Key computation: for $K_I^2=H^2\ominus IH^2$ and $A_g^I f=P_I(gf)$, the projective product space $X=\{\sum_kx_ky_k:\sum_k\|x_k\|_2\|y_k\|_2<\infty\}$ satisfies $X^*=\mathcal T(I)$ and ${}^*X=\mathcal T_c(I)$; the maps $S:X\to zH^1\cap K_{I^2}^1$, $f\mapsto If$, ${}^*S:C(\mathbb T)/(F_{I^2}\cap C(\mathbb T))\to\mathcal T_c(I)$, $[f]\mapsto A_{If}^I$, and $S^*:L^\infty/Q\to\mathcal T(I)$ identify their images with compact operators having symbols in $I C(\mathbb T)$ and bounded-symbol operators, so duality gives $\mathcal T_c(I)=\{A_{Ih}^I:h\in C(\mathbb T)\}$ if and only if every bounded $A_g^I$ has a bounded symbol.

records.title: Alfons Van Daele
records.summary: Alfons Van Daele, the polar decomposition of the antipode determines the modular structure of a locally compact quantum group and proves uniqueness of Haar weights. Key computation: regular representations satisfy $\Delta(x)=W^*(1\otimes x)W$ and $(\Delta\otimes\iota)W=W_{13}W_{23}$, while the closed antipode has $S((\iota\otimes\omega)W)=(\iota\otimes\omega)W^*$ and polar decomposition $S=R\tau_{-i/2}$; for two left Haar weights, $(K\otimes T_r)W_1=W_2^*(K\otimes T_r)$ implies $(1\otimes u_t)W_1(1\otimes u_t^*)=W_1$, hence $\Delta(u_t)=1\otimes u_t$ and $u_t$ is scalar, proving uniqueness up to scale; relative modular theory then produces the affiliated modular element $\delta$ with $\psi=\varphi(\delta^{1/2}\,\cdot\,\delta^{1/2})$, $\Delta(\delta)=\delta\otimes\delta$, and $\sigma_t'(x)=\delta^{it}\sigma_t(x)\delta^{-it}$.

records.title: Jingbo Xia
records.summary: Jingbo Xia, the Drury--Arveson space is the universal dilation space for commuting row contractions and its multiplier norm gives the correct multivariable von Neumann inequality. Key computation: for a strict commuting row contraction $A=(A_1,\ldots,A_n)$, the identity $\sum_{\alpha\in\mathbb Z_+^n}\frac{|\alpha|!}{\alpha!}A^\alpha(I-\sum_iA_iA_i^*)A^{*\alpha}=I$ makes $Zx=\sum_\alpha\frac{|\alpha|!}{\alpha!}(I-\sum_iA_iA_i^*)^{1/2}A^{*\alpha}x\,\zeta^\alpha$ an isometry into $H_n^2\otimes H$ satisfying $Zp(A^*)=(p(M_\zeta^*)\otimes I)Z$; hence $\|p(A)\|\leq\|p\|_{\operatorname{Mult}(H_n^2)}$, while for $\theta(\zeta)=\zeta_1\cdots\zeta_n$ one has $\|\theta^k\|_\infty=n^{-kn/2}$ but $\|\theta^k\|_{H_n^2}=((k!)^n/(nk)!)^{1/2}\asymp k^{(n-1)/4}n^{-kn/2}$, explicitly showing why the supremum norm cannot replace the multiplier norm for $n\ge2$.

records.title: Ilijas Farah
records.summary: Ilijas Farah, set-theoretic saturation sharply classifies ultrapowers of separable $C^*$-algebras: CH makes all nonprincipal ultrapowers isomorphic, while failure of CH yields the maximal number of isomorphism types. Key computation: countably saturated elementarily equivalent structures $C,D$ of density $\aleph_1$ are written as continuous chains $C=\bigcup_{\alpha<\omega_1}C_\alpha$ and $D=\bigcup_{\alpha<\omega_1}D_\alpha$; a transfinite back-and-forth constructs compatible elementary embeddings whose unions are inverse isomorphisms, so under CH, $A^{\mathcal U}\cong A^{\mathcal V}$ commuting with the diagonal copy of every separable $A$ and $A'\cap A^{\mathcal U}\cong A'\cap A^{\mathcal V}$; conversely, if CH fails, every separable infinite-dimensional $A$ has $2^{2^{\aleph_0}}$ nonisomorphic ultrapowers and as many nonisomorphic relative commutants.

records.title: Guoliang Yu
records.summary: Guoliang Yu, localization-algebra representatives refine higher indices to secondary rho invariants whose delocalized cyclic pairings recover Lott eta invariants. Key computation: partitions of unity on covers with mesh $<1/n$ localize $F=D(1+D^2)^{-1/2}$ to $F_n=\sum_k\sqrt{\phi_k^{(n)}}F\sqrt{\phi_k^{(n)}}$, and interpolation gives $\operatorname{propagation}(F_t)\to0$, defining $\operatorname{Index}_L(D)=[\exp(2\pi i(F_\bullet+1)/2)]\in K_1(C_L^*(\widetilde X)^G)$ with $e_*\operatorname{Index}_L(D)=\operatorname{Index}(D)$; when $D$ is invertible, splicing a trivialization to this path gives $\rho(D)\in K_*(C_{L,0}^*(\widetilde X)^G)$, and for a polynomial-growth conjugacy class $\langle h\rangle$, the explicit pairing $\tau_h(u)=(2\pi i)^{-1}\int_0^\infty\operatorname{tr}_h(\dot u(t)u(t)^{-1})dt$ satisfies $\tau_h(\rho(D))=\tfrac12\eta_{\langle h\rangle}(D)$.

records.title: Paolo Piazza (joint work with Hessel Posthuma
records.summary: Paolo Piazza (joint work with Hessel Posthuma, Yanli Song, and Xiang Tang), cyclic cocycles on Harish--Chandra Schwartz algebras give delocalized Atiyah--Patodi--Singer formulas for cocompact proper actions of real reductive groups. Key computation: the Connes--Moscovici heat projector $V(D)$ has entries in $\mathcal A_G^\infty(Y)$ and defines $\operatorname{Ind}_\infty(D)$; extending the semisimple orbital integral $\tau_g(f)=\int_{G/Z_G(g)}f(xgx^{-1})d(xZ_G(g))$ and applying Melrose's defect formula ${}^b\!\operatorname{Tr}[R,T]=(i/2\pi)\int_{\mathbb R}\operatorname{Tr}(\partial_\lambda I(R,\lambda)I(T,\lambda))d\lambda$ produces a relative cyclic cocycle, whose pairing yields $\langle\operatorname{Ind}_\infty(D),\tau_g^Y\rangle=\int_{Y_0^g}c^g\operatorname{AS}_g(Y_0)-\tfrac12\eta_g(D_{\partial Y})$ with $\eta_g(D)=(1/\sqrt\pi)\int_0^\infty\tau_g(D e^{-tD^2})dt/\sqrt t$.

records.title: Masoud Khalkhali
records.summary: Masoud Khalkhali, stable anti-Yetter--Drinfeld modules supply the coefficient objects that turn Hopf symmetries into cyclic modules and recover the Connes--Moscovici theory. Key computation: for a left $H$-module coalgebra $C$ and a right-left SAYD module $M$, the complex $C^n(C,M)=M\otimes_HC^{\otimes(n+1)}$ has cyclic operator $\tau_n(m\otimes c_0\otimes\cdots\otimes c_n)=m_{(0)}\otimes c_1\otimes\cdots\otimes c_n\otimes m_{(-1)}c_0$; the anti-Yetter--Drinfeld condition makes this operator descend through $\otimes_H$, and stability gives $\tau_n^{n+1}=\operatorname{id}$, hence a cocyclic module; modular pairs in involution $(\delta,\sigma)$ are exactly one-dimensional SAYD modules ${}^\sigma\mathbb C_\delta$, so taking $C=H$ recovers Connes--Moscovici Hopf cyclic cohomology and its characteristic map $\chi_\tau(h_1\otimes\cdots\otimes h_n)(a_0,\ldots,a_n)=\tau(a_0h_1(a_1)\cdots h_n(a_n))$.

records.title: Cong Xue
records.summary: Cong Xue, the compactly supported relative cohomology of shtuka stacks is ind-smooth and carries an unramified product Weil action. Key computation: geometric Satake defines $\mathcal H^j_{N,I,W}=R^jp_!\mathcal F_{N,I,W}$ on $(X\setminus N)^I$; the partial Frobenius maps $F_{\{i\}}:\operatorname{Frob}_{\{i\}}^*\mathcal H^j_{N,I,W}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal H^j_{N,I,W}$ compose to total Frobenius, so Drinfeld's lemma gives a $\operatorname{Weil}(\eta)^I$-action on the generic fiber, while Eichler--Shimura relations, constancy on mixed loci $(\eta)^{I_1}\times(v)^{I_2}$, and creation--annihilation (Zorro) operators make every specialization map $(\mathcal H^j_{N,I,W})_y\to(\mathcal H^j_{N,I,W})_x$ an isomorphism; hence $\mathcal H^j_{N,I,W}$ is ind-smooth and the action factors through $\operatorname{Weil}(X\setminus N)^I$.

records.title: Joachim Cuntz (joint with Guillermo Corti\~nas
records.summary: Joachim Cuntz (joint with Guillermo Corti\~nas, Ralf Meyer, and Georg Tamme), the Feigin--Tsygan theorem identifies periodic cyclic homology of any finite-type commutative algebra in characteristic zero with the de Rham cohomology of a smooth formal presentation. Key computation: for a smooth surjection $P\twoheadrightarrow A=P/J$ and the $J$-adic completion $P_J=\varprojlim_nP/J^n$, flatness of $P_J$ over the Noetherian ring $P$ and two completed bar resolutions give a quasi-isomorphism $P_J\otimes_P(C(P),b)\to(C(P_J),b)$ and therefore $HH_*(P_J)\cong P_J\otimes_PHH_*(P)\cong P_J\otimes_P\Omega_P^*$ by HKR; under this identification Connes' $B$ becomes $d$, while nilpotent invariance gives $HP_*(A)\cong HP_*(P_J)$, hence $HP_*(A)\cong HP_*(P_J)\cong H^*_{\mathrm{dR}}(P_J)=H^*_{\mathrm{inf}}(A)$.

records.title: Victor Nistor
records.summary: Victor Nistor, localization at conjugacy classes computes cyclic invariants of crossed products and reduces the periodic cyclic homology of a real algebraic group action to its maximal compact subgroup. Key computation: for a discrete action, the condition $\gamma_0\cdots\gamma_k\in\langle\gamma\rangle$ is preserved by Hochschild faces and cyclic permutation, giving $HH_k(A\rtimes\Gamma)\cong\bigoplus_{\langle\gamma\rangle}HH_k(A\rtimes\Gamma)_\gamma$ and $HH_*(A\rtimes\Gamma)_\gamma\cong HH_*(A\rtimes\Gamma)_{\mathfrak m_\gamma}$ for $\mathfrak m_\gamma=\{f\in C^\infty(\Gamma)^\Gamma:f(\gamma)=0\}$; for a connected real algebraic $G$ with maximal compact $K$ and $q=\dim(G/K)$, localization of the smooth convolution algebra then gives $HP_*(A\rtimes G)_{\mathfrak m}\cong HP_{*+q}(A\rtimes K)_{\mathfrak m}$, so every non-elliptic localization vanishes, while $HH_*(C^\infty(K))=C^\infty(K)^K$ and $HP_*(C^\infty(K))\cong C^\infty(K)^K\otimes\mathbb C[\sigma]$ with $|\sigma|=2$.

records.summary: Deepak Kumar Pradhan (joint with K. D. Deepak and Jaydeb Sarkar), partially isometric Toeplitz operators on the Hardy space of a polydisc are classified up to unitary equivalence as shifts, co-shifts, or direct sums of truncated shifts. Key computation: the Brown--Halmos relations $T_{z_i}^*TT_{z_i}=T$ force a partial-isometry symbol to depend on at most one of $z_i,\bar z_i$ for every $i$, and one obtains $T_\varphi=T_{\varphi_1}^*T_{\varphi_2}$ for inner $\varphi_1,\varphi_2\in H^\infty(\mathbb T^n)$ depending on disjoint variable sets; thus $D(T_\varphi)=\varphi_1H^2(\mathbb T^n)$, $R(T_\varphi)=\varphi_2H^2(\mathbb T^n)$, every $T_\varphi^m$ is again a partial isometry, and the Halmos--Wallen decomposition gives precisely the stated classification; moreover $[T_\varphi^*,T_\varphi]\ge0$ holds exactly when $\varphi$ is inner.

records.title: Orr Shalit
records.summary: Orr Shalit, quotients of the Drury--Arveson multiplier algebra are classified by the complex geometry of their multiplier varieties. Key computation: for $k(z,w)=(1-\langle z,w\rangle)^{-1}$ and $H_V=\overline{\operatorname{span}}\{k_\lambda:\lambda\in V\}$, one has $\mathcal M_V=\operatorname{Mult}(H_V)\cong\mathcal M_d/J_V$; an isometric algebra isomorphism induces $\alpha=(\varphi(z_1),\ldots,\varphi(z_d))\in\operatorname{Aut}(\mathbb B_d)$ through $\varphi^*(\rho_\lambda)=\rho_{\alpha(\lambda)}$, while conversely $Uk_\lambda=c_\lambda k_{\alpha(\lambda)}$ implements the algebra isomorphism, proving $\mathcal M_V\cong_{\mathrm{c.i.}}\mathcal M_W$ exactly when an automorphism of $\mathbb B_d$ maps $W$ onto $V$; for homogeneous varieties, algebraic isomorphism, similarity, biholomorphic equivalence, and equivalence under an invertible linear map of $\mathbb C^d$ are all equivalent.

records.summary: Robert T. W. Martin, noncommutative rational functions in the free Hardy space are exactly rational Szeg\H{o} kernels with stable minimal realizations, leading to finite free Blaschke products and finitely correlated Clark measures. Key computation: a minimal descriptor realization $r(Z)=(I_n\otimes b^*)(I_n\otimes I_N-\sum_jZ_j\otimes A_j)^{-1}(I_n\otimes c)$ belongs to $H_d^2$ exactly when $\operatorname{spr}(A)<1$, equivalently when $A$ is jointly similar to a strict row contraction $W$ and $r=K\{W,y,v\}$, equivalently $\mathbb B_d^{\mathrm{nc}}\subseteq\operatorname{Dom}r$; rational inner--outer factorization stays rational, every rational inner is a finite product of irreducible free Blaschke factors, and a contractive $b$ is rational exactly when its Clark functional $\mu_b$ is finitely correlated, with $b$ inner exactly when the compressed tuple $T_{\mu_b}=(\Pi_{\mu_b}^*|_{H_{\mu_b}})^*$ is a finite row co-isometry.

records.title: Rapha\'el Ponge
records.summary: Rapha\'el Ponge, measurable weak-trace-class operators are exactly Tauberian operators, giving a purely spectral formula for Connes' noncommutative integral and a semiclassical Weyl law for $L\log L$ potentials. Key computation: for $T\in\mathcal L_{1,\infty}$, $\tau(T)=[\{(\log N)^{-1}\sum_{k<N}\lambda_k(T)\}_N]\in\ell_\infty/c_0$ and every Dixmier trace is $\operatorname{Tr}_\omega=\omega\circ\tau$; independence of $\omega$ is equivalent to existence of $\lim_{N\to\infty}(\log N)^{-1}\sum_{k<N}\lambda_k(T)$, which equals $\mathop{\rlap{-}\!\int}T$; if $\int_M|V|\log(1+|V|)\,d\operatorname{vol}_g<\infty$, then $\Delta_g^{-n/4}V\Delta_g^{-n/4}\in\mathcal L_{1,\infty}$ and $\lim_{k\to\infty}k\lambda_k^\pm=c_n\int_MV_\pm\,d\operatorname{vol}_g$, hence $\mathop{\rlap{-}\!\int}\Delta_g^{-n/4}V\Delta_g^{-n/4}=c_n\int_MV\,d\operatorname{vol}_g$ and $\lim_{h\to0^+}h^nN^-(h^n\Delta_g+V)=c_n\int_MV_-\,d\operatorname{vol}_g$.

records.summary: Steven Amelotte (joint with Ben Briggs), componentwise almost-linear Stanley--Reisner resolutions classify a family of moment-angle manifolds as connected sums of sphere products. Key computation: $T\in BN_{(w,p,q)}(X,Y)$ precisely when $T=RB_wS$ for $S:X\to\ell^{q'}$ and $R:\ell^p\to Y$, with $Sx=(a_i(x))_i$, $R((\nu_i))=\sum_i\nu_i y_i$, and $B_w=\sum_{i\ge2}w_i e_i^*\otimes e_{i-1}$; the representation $T=\sum_{i\ge2}w_i a_i\otimes y_{i-1}$ gives $\|T\|_{(w,p,q)}=\inf\|R\|\,\|B_w\|\,\|S\|$, and $1/s=1/p'+1/q'$ makes $(BN_{(w,p,q)},\|\cdot\|_{(w,p,q)})$ an $s$-Banach operator ideal.

records.title: Nathan Wagner (joint with Cody Stockdale)
records.summary: Nathan Wagner (joint with Cody Stockdale), Berezin-transform boundary decay classifies compact Toeplitz operators on broad weighted Bergman spaces. Key computation: for $T_u f=P(uf)$ and normalized kernels $k_z(w)=(1-|z|^2)^{(n+1)/2}/(1-z\overline w)^{n+1}$, the Berezin transform $\widetilde T_u(z)=\langle T_uk_z,k_z\rangle$ satisfies $\widetilde T_u(z)\to0$ as $|z|\to1^-$ iff $T_u$ is compact on $A_\sigma^p$ when $\sigma\in B_p\cap RH_r$ and $\sigma^{1-p'}\in RH_r$; the underlying weighted Riesz--Kolmogorov criterion is $\lim_{r\to1^-}\sup_{f\in\mathcal F}\int_{r\mathbb B_n^c}|f|^p\sigma\,dV=0$, and sparse domination $|T_uf(z)|\lesssim\sum_{K\in\mathcal D}\langle|uf|\rangle_{\widehat K}\chi_{\widehat K}(z)$ yields boundedness for the larger $uB_p$ classes.

records.summary: Pascal Lef\`evre (joint with Tonie Far\`es), an explicit integral condition completely classifies absolutely summing composition operators between Bloch-type spaces and produces nuclear inner-symbol examples. Key computation: for $\varphi:\mathbb D\to\mathbb D$, $C_\varphi:\mathcal B^\mu\to\mathcal B^\beta$ is $p$-summing exactly when $\int_{\mathbb D}\sup_{z\in\mathbb D}\left(\frac{(1-|w|^2)^2}{|1-\overline w\varphi(z)|^2}\right)^p\left(\frac{(1-|z|^2)^\beta|\varphi'(z)|}{|1-\overline w\varphi(z)|^\mu}\right)^p\frac{dA(w)}{(1-|w|^2)^2}<\infty$; for lens maps $\varphi_\theta$, this gives $C_{\varphi_\theta}$ $p$-summing when $p>\theta/((\beta-1)(1-\theta))$ and nuclear when $\theta<1-1/\beta$, while suitable Blaschke products yield nuclear $C_\varphi$ on $\mathcal B^\beta$ for $\beta\ge1$.

records.title: Hugo J
records.summary: Hugo J. Woerdeman, positive structured completions of multilevel Toeplitz matrices classify stable multivariable autoregressive filters. Key computation: in two variables, Fourier data $c_k=\overline{c_{-k}}$ on $\mathbf n=\{0,\ldots,n_1\}\times\{0,\ldots,n_2\}$ come from a stable spectral density $|p(z_1,z_2)|^{-2}$ exactly when the missing coefficients can be chosen so that $T_{\mathbf n}=(c_{k-\ell})_{k,\ell\in\mathbf n}>0$ and $\operatorname{rank}(c_{k-\ell})_{k\in\{1,\ldots,n_1\}\times\{0,\ldots,n_2\},\,\ell\in\{0,\ldots,n_1\}\times\{1,\ldots,n_2\}}=n_1n_2$; for $c_{00}=1$ and $c_{01}=c_{10}=c_{11}=0.9$, the completion is explicitly $c_{1,-1}=0.81$, making the Toeplitz matrix positive definite and producing the stable filter.

Key computation: for $H=H^2(\beta)$ and $M(H,\varphi)=\{w:w(f\circ\varphi)\in H\ \forall f\in H\}$, one has $M(H^2,\varphi)\subseteq M(H,\varphi)$ and the sharp equivalences $M(H,\varphi)=H\Longleftrightarrow\|\varphi\|_\infty<1$ and $M(H,\varphi)=H^\infty\Longleftrightarrow\varphi$ is a finite Blaschke product; for $H^2$, the kernel estimate $\|K_a\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\sqrt{(1+|\varphi(a)|)/(1-|\varphi(a)|)}(1-|a|^2)^{-1/2}$ turns $M(H^2,\varphi)=H^\infty$ into $\sup_a(1-|\varphi(a)|)/(1-|a|)<\infty$, which is precisely the finite-Blaschke condition.

records.title: P
records.summary: P. Muthukumar, a Schur-class divisibility condition classifies exactly which Beurling subspaces are invariant under a composition operator. Key computation: for inner $\theta$ and analytic $\varphi:\mathbb D\to\mathbb D$, the conditions $C_\varphi(\theta H^2)\subseteq\theta H^2$ and $(\theta\circ\varphi)/\theta\in\mathcal S(\mathbb D)$ are equivalent; Douglas range inclusion rewrites this as $C_\varphi M_\theta=M_\theta X$, and evaluation of $X^*M_\theta^*=M_\theta^*C_\varphi^*$ on $K_w(z)=(1-\overline wz)^{-1}$ yields $X^*(\overline{\theta(w)}K_w)=\overline{\theta(\varphi(w))}K_{\varphi(w)}$, giving an equivalent bounded-kernel criterion and, for Blaschke $B$, the zero-multiplicity test $\operatorname{mult}_B(w)\le\operatorname{mult}_{B\circ\varphi}(w)$.

records.title: Francesco Fournier-Facio (joint with Bharatram Rangarajan)
records.summary: Francesco Fournier-Facio (joint with Bharatram Rangarajan), every lamplighter $\Gamma\wr\mathbb Z$ is Ulam stable with a linear estimate, which implies the same for Thompson's groups $F',F,T$ and embeds every countable group in a three-generated linearly Ulam-stable group. Key computation: an asymptotic homomorphism $\varphi_n:\Gamma\to U(k_n)$ defines $W=\prod_{n\to\omega}\mathfrak u(k_n)$ and an Ulam class $\alpha_\varphi\in H_a^2(\Gamma,W)$, with $\alpha_\varphi=0$ equivalent to a defect-diminishing correction $\operatorname{dist}(\varphi_n,\psi_n)=O_\omega(\operatorname{def}(\varphi_n))$ and $\operatorname{def}(\psi_n)=o_\omega(\operatorname{def}(\varphi_n))$; the highly ergodic Zimmer-amenable model for $\Gamma\wr\mathbb Z$ makes the relevant invariant cochain complex alternate $\operatorname{id}$ and $0$, killing every Ulam class, while the coamenable inclusion $F[a,b]\cong F< F'$ injects restriction on $H_a^2$ and transfers the vanishing to $F',F,T$.

Kudla, the numerical ring of special cycles on an orthogonal Shimura variety is determined by Fourier coefficients of pullbacks of Hilbert--Siegel Eisenstein series and depends only on the finite quadratic space. Key computation: the theta-form identity $[\theta(g_\tau';\varphi)]=\phi_n(\tau;\varphi)=\sum_{T\ge0}Z(T,\varphi)q^T$ and wedge compatibility $\varphi_\infty^{(n_1+n_2)}=\varphi_\infty^{(n_1)}\wedge\varphi_\infty^{(n_2)}$, followed by Siegel--Weil, give $\langle z(T_1,\varphi_1),z(T_2,\varphi_2)\rangle=A(T_1,T_2;\lambda_{V_f}(\varphi_1\otimes\varphi_2))$ for $n_1+n_2=m$ and $\langle z(T_1,\varphi_1)z(T_2,\varphi_2),z(T_3,\varphi_3)\rangle=A(T_1,T_2,T_3;\lambda_{V_f}(\varphi_1\otimes\varphi_2\otimes\varphi_3))$ for $n_1+n_2+n_3=m$; nondegeneracy determines multiplication, and matching Schwartz functions for $V(\mathbb A_f)\simeq V'(\mathbb A_f)$ yield an isometric graded-ring isomorphism $SC^\bullet(V)\simeq SC^\bullet(V')$.

records.title: Herbert Gangl
records.summary: Herbert Gangl, explicit polylogarithmic functional equations realize Zagier's polylogarithm conjecture through weight four and construct higher-weight analogues of the decisive motivic relation. Key computation: Bloch's map $\delta_2^F:\mathbb Z[F]\to\bigwedge^2F^\times$, $[x]\mapsto x\wedge(1-x)$, together with the exact sequence $0\to T(F)\to K_3(F)/K_3^M(F)\to B_2(F)\to0$, turns the single-valued dilogarithm into the regulator formula $\pi^{r_2}\zeta_F^*(-1)=q\det(\mathcal L_2(\xi_i^\sigma))_{i,\sigma}$; at weight four an explicit 122-term reduction $I_{3,1}(z,V(x,y))\equiv\sum_{i=1}^{122}c_i\operatorname{Li}_4(f_i(x,y,z))$ modulo lower-weight products supplies the $Q_4$ relation used by Goncharov--Rudenko to prove the conjecture for $m=4$, while the explicit quadruple ratio is a 368-orbit combination on eight points in $\mathbb P^3$ representing a nonzero class in $H^7(GL_4(\mathbb C),\mathbb R)$.

records.summary: Lisa Jeffrey (joint with Nan-Kuo Ho, Paul Selick, and Eugene Xia), Mayer--Vietoris decompositions compute the integral cohomology ring of the genus-two $SU(2)$ character variety with puncture monodromy $-I$ and identify its connected-sum type. records.title: Ron Donagi
records.summary: Ron Donagi, supermoduli is non-split and non-projected in genus at least five, while the super Mumford isomorphism constructs natural measures that extend across the vanishing-theta-null locus and, with Ramond punctures, across codimension at least two. Key computation: a supermanifold $S=(M,\mathcal O_S)$ has splitting obstruction $\omega\in H^1(M,T_M\otimes\bigwedge^2V^*)$, appearing as the third component of its super Atiyah class alongside the Atiyah classes of $T_+S$ and $T_-S$; for $\mathfrak M_g$, $\dim\mathfrak M_g=(3g-3\mid2g-2)$ with $T_+|_{[S]}=H^1(T_M)$ and $T_-|_{[S]}=H^1(T_M^{1/2})$, and restricting $\omega$ to a lifted family of odd-branched covers gives $\omega\ne0$ for $g\ge5$; the identity $\mathcal L_{3/2}\simeq\mathcal L_{1/2}^{5}$ defines the superstring measure, and a codimension-$\ge2$ Hartogs extension gives a natural measure on $\mathfrak M_{g,0,r}$ for $r\ge2$ Ramond punctures.

records.title: Meng Fai Lim
records.summary: Meng Fai Lim, the growth of \'etale wild kernels in multi-false-Tate towers is controlled by an Iwasawa-module rank, and its smaller-order growth is equivalent to the noncommutative Greenberg conjecture. Key computation: Poitou--Tate duality identifies $R_i(F)=WK_{2i}^{\mathrm{\acute et}}(F)^\vee$ with the kernel of $H^1(G_S(F),\mathbb Q_p/\mathbb Z_p(-i))\to\bigoplus_{v\in S}H^1(F_v,\mathbb Q_p/\mathbb Z_p(-i))$; Hochschild--Serre gives $\ker h_n=H^1(G_n,\mathbb Q_p/\mathbb Z_p(-i)(F_\infty))$ and $\operatorname{coker}h_n\subseteq H^2(G_n,\mathbb Q_p/\mathbb Z_p(-i)(F_\infty))$, yielding $e(R_i(F_\infty)^{G_n})-e(R_i(F_n))=O(np^{(d-2)n})$; if the cyclotomic $\mu$-conjecture holds, then $e(WK_{2i}^{\mathrm{\acute et}}(F_n))=\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb Z_p[[H]]}Y_i(F_\infty)\,np^{(d-1)n}+O(p^{(d-1)n})$, and vanishing of this rank is equivalent to $\operatorname{Gal}(K(F_\infty)/F_\infty)$ being pseudo-null.

records.title: Soumen Sarkar
records.summary: Soumen Sarkar, weighted Grassmann orbifolds have torsion-free integral cohomology concentrated in even degrees, and their integral equivariant cohomology is completely encoded by an orbifold GKM graph. Key computation: for $W=(w_1,\ldots,w_n)$ and $a\ge1$, $WGr(d,n)=M_d(n,d;\mathbb C)/{\sim_W}$ with $(a_1,\ldots,a_n)^t\sim_W(t^{w_1}a_1,\ldots,t^{w_n}a_n)^tT$ whenever $t^a=\det T$; its finite-quotient strata satisfy that $H_j(U(L)/G;\mathbb Z)$ has no $p$-torsion for $p\nmid|G|$, producing a torsion-free even-dimensional cellular filtration; each $WGr(d,n)$ is consequently a GKM orbifold and $H_{T^n}^*(WGr(d,n);\mathbb Z)\cong\{f:V(\Gamma)\to H^*(BT^n;\mathbb Z)\mid r_e\alpha(e)\text{ divides }f(s(e))-f(t(e))\}=H_{T^n}^*(\Gamma,\alpha,\theta)$.

records.title: Payman Eskandari (joint with Kumar Murty)
records.summary: Payman Eskandari (joint with Kumar Murty), the Ceresa cycle of every Fermat curve $F(p)$ of prime degree $p>7$ has infinite order modulo rational equivalence, for every base point. Key computation: quadratic iterated integrals give $E_e^\infty\in\operatorname{Ext}((H^1)^{\otimes3},\mathbb Q(-1))$, and for a correspondence $Z$ the Darmon--Rotger--Sols formula is $\xi_Z^{-1}(E_e^\infty)=(\int_\Delta\xi_Z)(\infty-e)-P_Z$; taking $Z$ as the graph of $(x,y,z)\mapsto(-y,z,x)$ on $F(p)$ gives fixed points $Q=(\eta,\eta^{-1},1)$ and $\bar Q=(\eta^{-1},\eta,1)$ and hence $P_Z=Q+\bar Q-2e$, which Gross--Rohrlich proves has infinite order while $\infty-e$ is torsion; thus $E_e^\infty\ne0$, its $H^1\otimes\xi_\Delta$ component $-2g\infty+2e+K$ is torsion, and Harris--Pulte identifies the remaining component with $\tfrac12AJ(F(p)_e-F(p)_e^-)$, forcing the Abel--Jacobi image, and therefore the Ceresa cycle, to be nonzero.

records.title: Avi Zeff
records.summary: Avi Zeff, prismatic cohomology of quasiregular semiperfectoid rings is computed in degree zero and its Nygaard completion recovers the even homotopy of $\mathrm{THH}$, $\mathrm{TC}^-$, and $\mathrm{TP}$. Key computation: the initial prism $(\Delta_R^{\mathrm{init}},(d))$ gives $\Delta_{R/A}=\Delta_R=\Delta_R^{\mathrm{init}}$ and $N^{\ge i}\Delta_R=\varphi^{-1}(d^i\Delta_R)$; after Nygaard completion, $\pi_{2*}\mathrm{THH}(R)=N^*\widehat\Delta_R\{*\}$, $\pi_{2*}\mathrm{TC}^-(R)=N^{\ge *}\widehat\Delta_R\{*\}$, and $\pi_{2*}\mathrm{TP}(R)=\widehat\Delta_R\{*\}$, with all odd homotopy groups vanishing.

records.title: David Mart\'inez-Carpena (with Carles Casacuberta and Javier J
records.summary: David Mart\'inez-Carpena (with Carles Casacuberta and Javier J. Guti\'errez), presentable $\infty$-categories are exactly the categories of models of limit $\infty$-sketches. Key computation: for a limit $\infty$-sketch $\Sigma=(A,L)$, $\operatorname{Mod}(\Sigma)=\{F:A\to\mathcal S\mid F(\alpha)\text{ is limiting for every }\alpha\in L\}$ is presentable, and conversely every presentable $\infty$-category $\mathcal C$ admits a normal $\Sigma$ with $\mathcal C\simeq\operatorname{Mod}(\Sigma)$; concretely, the cones $\alpha_n$ on $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ impose $F_n\simeq F_1\times_{F_0}\cdots\times_{F_0}F_1$, so their models are Segal spaces, while adjoining the univalence cone produces complete Segal spaces.

records.title: Andr\'e Joyal
records.summary: Andr\'e Joyal, the free bicompletion of a locally small category is characterized intrinsically by softness together with atomic and co-atomic generators. Key computation: softness requires the canonical square from $\operatorname*{colim}_I\operatorname*{lim}_J\mathcal E(A_i,B_j)$ to $\mathcal E(\operatorname*{lim}_I A_i,\operatorname*{colim}_J B_j)$ to be a pushout; hence every $f:\prod_{i\in I}A_i\to\coprod_{j\in J}B_j$ factors through some projection $\prod_iA_i\to A_i$, some inclusion $B_j\to\coprod_jB_j$, or both, and $\eta:K\to\Lambda(K)$ is the free bicompletion precisely when $\Lambda(K)$ is bicomplete and soft, $\eta$ is fully faithful and generating, and each $\eta(A)$ is atomic and co-atomic.

records.title: Nathanael Arkor and Dylan McDermott
records.summary: Nathanael Arkor and Dylan McDermott, the algebras of any relative monad rooted at a dense functor are reconstructed as a pullback along the corresponding nerve, subsuming standard nerve theorems. Key computation: for $j:A\to E$ dense and a $j$-relative monad $T$ with $\operatorname{Kl}(T)(x,y)=E(jx,ty)$, the square $\operatorname{Alg}(T)\to\widehat{\operatorname{Kl}(T)}$ over $E\xrightarrow{n_j}\widehat A$, where $n_j(e)=E(j-,e)$, is a pullback in $\operatorname{Cat}$; thus $\operatorname{Kl}(T)\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Alg}(T)$ is dense, and for an ordinary monad the analogous square is a pullback exactly when $T$ is $j$-ary, recovering algebraic theories and the Segal-nerve classification of categories.

records.title: Joanna Ko
records.summary: Joanna Ko, enhanced simplicial categories of $(\infty,1)$-categories with specified limits and lax morphisms admit the higher limit constructions needed for Eilenberg--Moore objects. Key computation: $J\text{-}\operatorname{Lim}$ admits rigged $n$-inserters, so in particular comma objects whose projections preserve and jointly reflect $J$-shaped limits; since a loose homotopy-coherent monad's Eilenberg--Moore object is assembled from simplicial powers, rigged $n$-inserters, and limits of countable chains of tight isofibrations, $\operatorname{Lali}(\mathcal K)$ admits such Eilenberg--Moore objects and its forgetful functor is exact and detects exactness, recovering that $U:T\text{-}\operatorname{Alg}\to A$ lifts $J$-limits even when $T$ does not preserve them.

records.title: Seerp Roald Koudenburg
records.summary: Seerp Roald Koudenburg, formal Day convolution lifts Yoneda morphisms and yields a monoidal double Grothendieck correspondence. Key computation: a lax $T$-algebra $(A,\alpha)$ and Yoneda morphism $y:A\to\widehat A$ lift, when the pointwise weak composite $\alpha_*\odot Ty_*$ exists, to a lax $T$-algebra structure on $\widehat A$ for which $y$ is pseudo-$T$, giving $\widehat A(y,-):(\operatorname{Lax}\text{-}T\text{-}\operatorname{Mor}(B,\widehat A))\simeq(T\text{-}\operatorname{Mor}(A,B))$; for $y:A\to\operatorname{Set}^{A^{\mathrm{op}}}$ this constructs Day convolution, while for $Y:1\to\operatorname{Span}(\operatorname{Cat})$ it identifies lax monoidal lax double functors $G:(B,\otimes)\to(\operatorname{Span}(\operatorname{Cat}),\times)$ with lax monoidal double split opfibrations $\int G\to B$.

records.title: Fosco Loregian
records.summary: Fosco Loregian, bicategorical Moore machines are models of a finite weighted-limit sketch and their universal machine is computed by a right Kan extension. Key computation: classical machines arise from pullbacks $\operatorname{Mly}(F,B)=\operatorname{Alg}(F)\times_K(F/B)$ and $\operatorname{Mre}(F,B)=\operatorname{Alg}(F)\times_K(K/B)$; in a bicategory, a fixed-input/output biMoore machine fills the $2$-cells $\delta:e\circ i\Rightarrow e$ and $\sigma:e\Rightarrow o$, and its terminal object is $\operatorname{Ran}_{i^\sharp}(o)$ along the free monad $i^\sharp:A\to A$, recovering $[A^*,B]$ in the one-object closed-monoidal case and extending the construction to $(T,V)$-profunctors.

records.title: Arne Mertens (joint with Wendy Lowen)
records.summary: Arne Mertens (joint with Wendy Lowen), necklace-parametrized templicial objects define quasi-categories enriched in a non-cartesian monoidal category and explicitly compute left adjoints to enriched nerve functors. Key computation: the nerve has $N_V(C)_n=C_1\otimes_{C_0}\cdots\otimes_{C_0}C_1$ and comultiplications $\mu_{k,l}:X_{k+l}\to X_k\otimes_{X_0}X_l$ indexed by inclusions $\Delta^k\vee\Delta^l\hookrightarrow\Delta^{k+l}$; if $\pi D\simeq\operatorname{Lan}_\iota D'$, then $\pi(L_DX(a,b))\simeq\coprod_{T\in\operatorname{Nec}}F(X_T^{\mathrm{nd}}(a,b))\otimes D'(T)$, yielding for Lurie's dg nerve $L_{\mathrm{dg}}(X)_n(a,b)\simeq\bigoplus_{\dim T=n}k\!\cdot\!X_T^{\mathrm{nd}}(a,b)$.

records.title: Samarpita Ray (joint with Abhishek Banerjee and Mamta Balodi)
records.summary: Samarpita Ray (joint with Abhishek Banerjee and Mamta Balodi), representations of coalgebras have Grothendieck categories of cis- and trans-comodules, with cartesian subcategories serving as coalgebraic analogues of quasi-coherent sheaves. Key computation: for $C:X\to\operatorname{Coalg}$ with right-semiperfect values, a map $V\to M_x$ from a finite-dimensional projective generates $N_y=\operatorname{Im}(\bigoplus_{\beta:x\to y}\beta_*V\to M_y)$ with $|N|\le\kappa=\sup\{\aleph_0,|\operatorname{Mor}X|,|K|\}$, and every $M$ is a sum of such $N$, proving $\operatorname{Com}^{\mathrm{cs}}\!\text{-}C$ is Grothendieck; if $C$ is quasi-finite then $\alpha_!=H_{C_y}(C_x,-)\dashv\alpha^*$ gives the corresponding Grothendieck classification for $\operatorname{Com}^{\mathrm{tr}}\!\text{-}C$, while semiperfect $C$ makes $\operatorname{Com}^{\mathrm{cs}}\!\text{-}C$ a hereditary torsion class in $C^*\text{-}\operatorname{Mod}^{\mathrm{tr}}$.

records.title: Brais Ramos P\'erez
records.summary: Brais Ramos P\'erez, modules over invertible Hopf-algebra $1$-cocycles are equivalent to modules over the associated Hopf braces. Key computation: an invertible $1$-cocycle is a coalgebra isomorphism $\pi:A\to H$ satisfying $\pi\circ\mu_A=\mu_H\circ(\pi\otimes\varphi_H)\circ(\delta_A\otimes\pi)$; it produces the brace $H_\pi=Q(\pi,\varphi_H)$, and the functor $H_\pi:(\pi,\varphi_H)\text{-}\operatorname{Mod}\to H_\pi\text{-}\operatorname{Mod}$ sends $(M,N,\varphi_M,\phi_M,\varphi_N,\gamma)$ to $(M,\phi_M,\gamma\circ\varphi_N\circ(\pi^{-1}\otimes\gamma^{-1}))$, with inverse $M_{(\pi,\operatorname{id}_H)}\circ G_{H_\pi}$, so the composites are $\operatorname{id}_{H_\pi\text{-}\operatorname{Mod}}$ and naturally isomorphic to $\operatorname{id}_{(\pi,\varphi_H)\text{-}\operatorname{Mod}}$.

records.title: Ivan Limonchenko (joint with Rade \v{Z}ivaljevi\'c and Matvey Sergeev)
records.summary: Ivan Limonchenko (joint with Rade \v{Z}ivaljevi\'c and Matvey Sergeev), flag Bier spheres are classified by four families of simple polytopes, and every Bier sphere canonically determines smooth moment-angle and toric manifolds. Key computation: every flag $\operatorname{Bier}(K)$ is the nerve of $I^n$, $I^n\times Q_5$, $I^n\times Q_6$, or $I^n\times P_4$; moreover $s_{\mathbb R}(\operatorname{Bier}(K))=s(\operatorname{Bier}(K))=m+1$, and the cones $C(\sigma,\tau)=\mathbb R_{\ge0}\langle-e_p,e_q\mid p\in\sigma,\ q'\in\tau\rangle$ form a complete regular fan $\Sigma(K)\subset\mathbb R^{m-1}$, producing the smooth manifolds $Z_{\operatorname{Bier}(K)}^{3m-1}$ and $X_{\Sigma(K)}^{2(m-1)}$.

records.title: Daisuke Kishimoto (joint with Kouyemon Iriye)
records.summary: Daisuke Kishimoto (joint with Kouyemon Iriye), a triangulation of an $\mathbb F$-orientable manifold is $\mathbb F$-Golod if and only if it is $\mathbb F$-tight. Hajac (joint work with Mariusz Tobolski), suitable graph and path homomorphisms make Leavitt path algebras contravariant and graph $C^*$-algebras covariant, yielding pushout-to-pullback theorems for quantum spaces. records.summary: Alfons Van Daele, a locally compact quantum group defined by central Haar weights on a $C^*$-algebra canonically yields a faithful von Neumann algebraic locally compact quantum group. Key computation: a lower-semicontinuous semifinite weight extends by $\widetilde\varphi(x)=\sup_{\omega\le\varphi}\omega(x)$ to a normal weight on $A^{**}$, and Haar invariance $\varphi((\omega\otimes\iota)\Delta(a))=\omega(1)\varphi(a)$ implies that the support projections $e$ and $f$ of the extended left and right weights satisfy $\widetilde\Delta(1-e)(1\otimes(1-e))=0$, hence $f(1-e)=e(1-f)=0$ and $e=f$; cutting down to $M=A^{**}e$ gives $\Delta_0(x)=\widetilde\Delta(x)(e\otimes e)$ with faithful invariant restrictions $\varphi_0,\psi_0$, so $(M,\Delta_0)$ is the associated von Neumann algebraic quantum group.

records.title: Stevo Todorcevic
records.summary: Stevo Todorcevic, the Ne\v{s}et\v{r}il--R\'odl ordered expansion canonizes finite-arity relations on the random graph and identifies the universal minimal flow of its automorphism group. Key computation: for a finite graph $A$ on $\{0,\ldots,k-1\}$, $C_A=\operatorname{Emb}(A,R)=\{\bar x\in\mathbb N^{(k)}:(i,j)\in E_A\Longleftrightarrow(x_i,x_j)\in R\}$ splits under a homogeneous order $<^*$ into $C_A^\sigma=\{\bar x\in C_A:x_{\sigma(0)}<^*\cdots<^*x_{\sigma(k-1)}\}$; every $S\subseteq\mathbb N^{(k)}$ is constant on each $C_A^\sigma$ after restriction to an arbitrarily large finite induced subgraph, all $k!$ classes remain essential, and this Ramsey-plus-ordering computation makes the natural action $\operatorname{Aut}(R)\curvearrowright\operatorname{LO}(\mathbb N)$ minimal and universal.

records.title: Morris Ang
records.summary: Morris Ang, Gaussian multiplicative chaos constructs Liouville quantum gravity surfaces and the DOZZ three-point function computes the universal critical-percolation three-point connectivity constant. records.title: Liat Kessler (joint work with Pranav Chakravarthy
records.summary: Liat Kessler (joint work with Pranav Chakravarthy, River Chiang, and Martin Pinsonnault), equivariant symplectic blowups of a Hamiltonian circle four-manifold at a fixed component are connected from deformation to isotopy using decorated-graph classification and inflation. Key computation: an embedded $J$-holomorphic surface $Z$ produces $J$-taming forms in the classes $[\omega_t]=[\omega]+t\lambda\operatorname{PD}[Z]$ for $0\le\lambda<T$, where $T=\infty$ if $Z\cdot Z\ge0$ and $T=\omega(Z)/(-Z\cdot Z)$ otherwise; applying this family inflation to two $S^1$-equivariant blowups of equal size, whose Karshon decorated graphs coincide, changes the invariant deformation to a cohomologous path, and equivariant Moser then writes $\omega_t=\phi_t^*\omega_0$, giving equivariant isotopy.

records.title: Stevo Todorcevic
records.summary: Stevo Todorcevic, analytic $n^*$-gaps have a finite basis of minimal equivalence types, obtained by canonizing their tree presentations. Key computation: for gaps $\Gamma$ on $N$ and $\Delta$ on $M$, $\Gamma\le\Delta$ is witnessed by an injection $\phi:N\to M$ carrying $\Gamma_i$ into $\Delta_i$ and $\Gamma_i^\perp$ into $\Delta_i^\perp$; the tree partition theorem produces, from any non-separated analytic family $\Gamma=\{\Gamma_i:i<n\}$, a permutation $\varepsilon:n\to n$ and injection $u:n^{<\omega}\to N$ with $u[X]\in\Gamma_{\varepsilon(i)}$ for every chain $X$ of type $[i]$, reducing every analytic gap to one of finitely many minimal types--exactly five for $n=2$ up to permutation--and yielding the sharp intersection numbers $J(1),\ldots,J(7)=1,8,61,480,3881,31976,266981$.

records.title: Jeff Achter
records.summary: Jeff Achter, cyclic covers turn moduli of genus-$4$ curves, plane quartics, and five marked points on $\mathbb P^1$ into arithmetic period maps to unitary Shimura varieties. Key computation: for a canonical genus-$4$ curve $C=Q\cap S\subset\mathbb P^3$, the triple cover $v:Z\to Q$ branched along $C$ is a K3 surface; the inverse images $N_i=v^{-1}(M_i)$ of the two rulings satisfy $(N_1,N_2)=3$, so $U(3)=\mathbb ZN_1+\mathbb ZN_2\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Pic}(Z)$ and the deck $\mu_3$-action produces $(Z,\alpha,\rho)\in\mathcal R_{(L_4,\chi_4)}$. Over $\mathbb Z[\zeta_3,1/6]$, $\kappa_4:\mathcal R_{(L_4,\chi_4)}\to\mathcal N_4$ induces an isomorphism on coarse moduli spaces and $\tau_4$ is an open immersion into $\operatorname{Sh}(L_4,\chi_4)$.

records.title: Yousheng Shi
records.summary: Yousheng Shi, derived intersections of Kudla--Rapoport divisors on ramified unitary Rapoport--Zink spaces equal a corrected derivative of local representation densities in ranks $n\le3$. Key computation: blowing up the isolated singularities of $\mathcal N_n^{\mathrm{Pap}}$ gives the regular semistable Kr\'amer model $\mathcal N_n^{\mathrm{Kra}}$, and for $L=\langle x_1,\ldots,x_n\rangle$ the intersection is $\operatorname{Int}(L)=\chi(\mathcal N_n,\mathcal O_{\mathcal Z(x_1)}\otimes^{\mathbf L}\cdots\otimes^{\mathbf L}\mathcal O_{\mathcal Z(x_n)})$. Solving the triangular system $2\alpha'(M_j,M)/\alpha(M,M)+\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}c_i\alpha(M_j,M_i)=0$ produces the correction terms and the formula $\operatorname{Int}(L)=2\alpha'(L,M)/\alpha(M,M)+\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}c_i\alpha(L,M_i)$; for $n=3$, the difference-cycle identity $\mathbb L D^{\mathrm{Kra}}(L)\cdot\mathcal Z^{\mathrm{Kra}}(x)=\beta(L\oplus\{x\},M)(2)$ reduces the proof inductively to $n=2$.

records.summary: Mahesh Kakde (joint with Samit Dasgupta), the integral Gross--Stark theorem proves the strong Brumer conjecture and gives a $p$-adic class-field construction from Brumer--Stark units. Key computation: the Stickelberger element satisfies $\chi(\Theta_q^{H/F})=L_R(\chi^{-1},0)(1-\chi^{-1}(q)Nq)$ and $\Theta_q^{H/F}\in\operatorname{Fitt}_{\mathbb Z[G]}(\operatorname{Cl}_q(H)^{\vee,-})$; hence for a split prime $\mathfrak p$ its class is principalized by the unique unit $u$ with $\sum_{\sigma\in G}[\sigma^{-1}]\operatorname{ord}_{\mathfrak P}(\sigma u)=\Theta_q^{H/F}$. For $S=\{\mathfrak p_i:\chi(\mathfrak p_i)=1\}$, the proved Gross--Stark formula computes the leading term $L_p^{(r)}(\chi\omega,0)/(r!L(\chi,0)\prod_{\chi(\mathfrak p)\ne1}(1-\chi(\mathfrak p)))=\det(\log_pN_{F_{\mathfrak p_i}/\mathbb Q_p}u_j)/\det(\operatorname{ord}_{\mathfrak P_i}u_j)$, while in rank one $\chi(\Theta_q^{H_{\mathrm{cyc}}/F})=\sum_{\sigma\in G}\chi(\sigma^{-1})(\operatorname{rec}(\sigma u)-1)$ in $I/I^2$.

records.summary: Taras Panov, polyhedral products classify when graph-product classifying spaces are aspherical and when commutator subgroups of right-angled Coxeter groups are free or one-relator. records.title: Nima Hoda
records.summary:
Nima Hoda, bisimplices give a canonical higher-dimensional completion of complete bipartite subgraphs, and filling every $K_{m+1,n+1}$ in a locally finite quadric complex produces a contractible complex with unchanged $2$-skeleton. Key computation: the $(m,n)$-bisimplex $
abla\!\Delta^{m,n}$ is built inductively by placing one $
abla\!\Delta^{m',n'}$ on each proper $K_{m'+1,n'+1}$ and then attaching an $(m+n)$-cell to $\partial
abla\!\Delta^{m,n}$. An explicit discrete Morse matching on this boundary has exactly two critical cells, so $\partial
abla\!\Delta^{m,n}\simeq S^{m+n-1}$; the link of every cell has the same two-critical-cell matching, hence induction makes every link a sphere, and the generalized Poincar'e theorem upgrades the homotopy equivalence to $\partial
abla\!\Delta^{m,n}\cong S^{m+n-1}$, proving $
abla\!\Delta^{m,n}\cong B^{m+n}$.

records.title: Victor Buchstaber
records.summary: Victor Buchstaber, partially framed manifolds give explicit generators and characteristic numbers for complex bordism and compute the complex cobordism of $\Omega SU(2)\simeq\Omega S^3$. Key computation: the hypersurface $M_{2n}\subset(\mathbb{CP}^{1}_{*})^{n+1}$ Poincar\'e dual to $\eta_1\otimes\cdots\otimes\eta_{n+1}$ generates $(\mathrm{fr}(1),U)_{2n}\cong\mathbb Z$ and has $\operatorname{Td}(M_{2n})=(-1)^n$, $c_n(M_{2n})=(-1)^n(n+1)!$, and $\tau(M_{2n})=4^{n+1}(4^{n+1}-1)B_{2n+2}/(2n+2)$. The James equivalence $J(S^2)\simeq\Omega S^3$ then yields $U_*(\Omega S^3)\cong\Omega_U[w]$ and $U^*(\Omega S^3)\cong\Omega_U[[b_2,b_4,\ldots]]/(b_2^n-n!b_{2n})_{n\ge2}$, with $b_{2i}b_{2j}=\binom{i+j}{i}b_{2(i+j)}$ and $\varphi_U^*u=b_2+\sum_{n\ge1}[M_{2n}]b_{2n+2}$.

records.title: Luis Scoccola
records.summary: Luis Scoccola, the Gromov--Hausdorff distance is universally characterized as a quotient interleaving distance, making homotopy and density filtrations stable functors of metric data. Key computation: for pseudometric spaces, let $d_I(P,Q)$ be the infimum of $\delta$ admitting inverse set maps that increase distances by at most $\delta$, and quotient by zigzags of surjective distance-preserving maps; the slides prove $(d_I)/{\simeq}=2d_{\mathrm{GH}}$. Consequently the Vietoris--Rips functor is $2$-Lipschitz into homotopy interleaving distance, while the bifiltration $\operatorname{KDF}(X)(s,k)=\{x\in X:\int_XK(d_X(x,x')/s)\,d\mu_X(x')\ge k\}$ is uniformly continuous from Gromov--Hausdorff--Prokhorov distance to Gromov--Hausdorff interleaving distance; for full-support $X$ and iid samples $X_n$, $\operatorname{KDF}(X_n)\to\operatorname{KDF}(X)$ in probability.

records.title: Von Neumann Algebra Automorphisms and Time-Thermodynamics Relation in General Covariant Quantum Theories
records.summary: Connes and Rovelli formulate the thermal-time hypothesis. Section 2 distinguishes the state-dependent modular automorphism group from the canonical state-independent flow in $\operatorname{Out}(M)$.
records.content: Connes and Rovelli formulate the thermal-time hypothesis. Section 2 distinguishes the state-dependent modular automorphism group from the canonical state-independent flow in $\operatorname{Out}(M)$.

records.title: Some Entanglement Properties of Quantum Field Theory
records.summary: Witten's accessible account of operator-algebraic entanglement. Section IV.B, equation (IV.35), computes finite-dimensional modular flow as $a\mapsto\rho^{is}a\rho^{-is}$.
records.content: Witten's accessible account of operator-algebraic entanglement. Section IV.B, equation (IV.35), computes finite-dimensional modular flow as $a\mapsto\rho^{is}a\rho^{-is}$.

records.title: Structure of von Neumann Algebras of Type III
records.summary: Takesaki's master-class notes on type III structure and flow of weights. Pages 31--33 compute modular automorphisms of weighted $2\times2$ and $3\times3$ matrix blocks and their periods.
records.content: Takesaki's master-class notes on type III structure and flow of weights. Pages 31--33 compute modular automorphisms of weighted $2\times2$ and $3\times3$ matrix blocks and their periods.

records.title: Basic Noncommutative Geometry
records.summary: Khalkhali's introductory text. Examples 2.1.5 and 2.5.9 compute the irrational Kronecker foliation's transverse groupoid $\mathbb{T}\rtimes_\theta\mathbb{Z}$ and identify its algebra with the noncommutative torus $A_\theta$.
records.content: Khalkhali's introductory text. Examples 2.1.5 and 2.5.9 compute the irrational Kronecker foliation's transverse groupoid $\mathbb{T}\rtimes_\theta\mathbb{Z}$ and identify its algebra with the noncommutative torus $A_\theta$.

records.title: Perfectoid Spaces
records.summary: Perfectoid Spaces. Introduces perfectoid fields and perfectoid spaces, proves the tilting equivalence between perfectoid spaces over $K$ and over its tilt $K^\flat$ in characteristic $p$, and deduces the weight-monodromy conjecture for complete intersections.
records.content: Perfectoid Spaces. Introduces perfectoid fields and perfectoid spaces, proves the tilting equivalence between perfectoid spaces over $K$ and over its tilt $K^\flat$ in characteristic $p$, and deduces the weight-monodromy conjecture for complete intersections.

records.title: p-Adic Hodge Theory for Rigid-Analytic Varieties
records.summary: p-Adic Hodge Theory for Rigid-Analytic Varieties. Develops the pro-étale site and the period sheaves $\mathbb{B}_{\mathrm{dR}}^+$ on rigid-analytic varieties, proving the de Rham comparison and degeneration of the Hodge–de Rham spectral sequence for proper smooth rigid spaces.
records.content: p-Adic Hodge Theory for Rigid-Analytic Varieties. Develops the pro-étale site and the period sheaves $\mathbb{B}_{\mathrm{dR}}^+$ on rigid-analytic varieties, proving the de Rham comparison and degeneration of the Hodge–de Rham spectral sequence for proper smooth rigid spaces.

records.title: Étale Cohomology of Diamonds
records.summary: Étale Cohomology of Diamonds. Defines diamonds as quotients of perfectoid spaces by pro-étale equivalence relations and builds the six-functor formalism for étale cohomology of diamonds and small v-stacks.
records.content: Étale Cohomology of Diamonds. Defines diamonds as quotients of perfectoid spaces by pro-étale equivalence relations and builds the six-functor formalism for étale cohomology of diamonds and small v-stacks.

records.title: Integral p-Adic Hodge Theory
records.summary: Integral p-Adic Hodge Theory. Constructs the $A_{\mathrm{inf}}$-cohomology of proper smooth formal schemes over $\mathcal{O}_C$ interpolating étale, crystalline and de Rham cohomology, and bounds torsion in étale cohomology by torsion in de Rham cohomology.
records.content: Integral p-Adic Hodge Theory. Constructs the $A_{\mathrm{inf}}$-cohomology of proper smooth formal schemes over $\mathcal{O}_C$ interpolating étale, crystalline and de Rham cohomology, and bounds torsion in étale cohomology by torsion in de Rham cohomology.

records.title: Topological Hochschild Homology and Integral p-Adic Hodge Theory
records.summary: Topological Hochschild Homology and Integral p-Adic Hodge Theory. Recovers $A_{\mathrm{inf}}$-cohomology and crystalline cohomology from topological Hochschild and topological cyclic homology via the motivic filtration on $\mathrm{THH}$, $\mathrm{TC}^-$ and $\mathrm{TP}$ of quasisyntomic rings.
records.content: Topological Hochschild Homology and Integral p-Adic Hodge Theory. Recovers $A_{\mathrm{inf}}$-cohomology and crystalline cohomology from topological Hochschild and topological cyclic homology via the motivic filtration on $\mathrm{THH}$, $\mathrm{TC}^-$ and $\mathrm{TP}$ of quasisyntomic rings.

records.title: Absolute Prismatic Cohomology
records.summary: Absolute Prismatic Cohomology. Studies the absolute prismatic cohomology of $p$-adic formal schemes via the Cartier–Witt stack $\mathrm{WCart}$, proving comparisons with syntomic cohomology and constructing prismatic F-gauges.
records.content: Absolute Prismatic Cohomology. Studies the absolute prismatic cohomology of $p$-adic formal schemes via the Cartier–Witt stack $\mathrm{WCart}$, proving comparisons with syntomic cohomology and constructing prismatic F-gauges.

records.title: The Prismatization of p-Adic Formal Schemes
records.summary: The Prismatization of p-Adic Formal Schemes. Constructs the prismatization $X^{\Delta}$ of a bounded $p$-adic formal scheme as a stack over $\mathrm{WCart}$ whose quasi-coherent cohomology recovers absolute prismatic cohomology.
records.content: The Prismatization of p-Adic Formal Schemes. Constructs the prismatization $X^{\Delta}$ of a bounded $p$-adic formal scheme as a stack over $\mathrm{WCart}$ whose quasi-coherent cohomology recovers absolute prismatic cohomology.

records.title: Prismatization
records.summary: Prismatization. Geometrizes prismatic cohomology through the stacks $\Sigma$, $\Sigma'$ and $\Sigma''$ built from Witt vectors, describing the Hodge–Tate divisor and the Breuil–Kisin twists stack-theoretically.
records.content: Prismatization. Geometrizes prismatic cohomology through the stacks $\Sigma$, $\Sigma'$ and $\Sigma''$ built from Witt vectors, describing the Hodge–Tate divisor and the Breuil–Kisin twists stack-theoretically.

records.title: The Pro-Étale Topology for Schemes
records.summary: The Pro-Étale Topology for Schemes. Defines the pro-étale site of a scheme, shows it is locally weakly contractible and replete, and uses it to give a clean definition of $\ell$-adic sheaves and the constructible derived category.
records.content: The Pro-Étale Topology for Schemes. Defines the pro-étale site of a scheme, shows it is locally weakly contractible and replete, and uses it to give a clean definition of $\ell$-adic sheaves and the constructible derived category.

records.title: The arc-Topology
records.summary: The arc-Topology. Introduces the arc-topology on qcqs schemes, detected by rank-one valuation rings, and proves arc-descent for étale cohomology with torsion coefficients and for perfect schemes.
records.content: The arc-Topology. Introduces the arc-topology on qcqs schemes, detected by rank-one valuation rings, and proves arc-descent for étale cohomology with torsion coefficients and for perfect schemes.

records.title: Relative p-Adic Hodge Theory: Foundations
records.summary: Relative p-Adic Hodge Theory: Foundations. Develops relative $(\varphi, \Gamma)$-modules over adic spaces, perfectoid algebras and the correspondence between étale local systems and $\varphi$-modules over relative Robba rings.
records.content: Relative p-Adic Hodge Theory: Foundations. Develops relative $(\varphi, \Gamma)$-modules over adic spaces, perfectoid algebras and the correspondence between étale local systems and $\varphi$-modules over relative Robba rings.

records.title: An Introduction to the Theory of p-Adic Representations
records.summary: An Introduction to the Theory of p-Adic Representations. Survey of Fontaine's rings $\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{cris}}, \mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{st}}, \mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{dR}}$, $(\varphi, \Gamma)$-modules, and the proof that de Rham representations are potentially semistable.
records.content: An Introduction to the Theory of p-Adic Representations. Survey of Fontaine's rings $\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{cris}}, \mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{st}}, \mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{dR}}$, $(\varphi, \Gamma)$-modules, and the proof that de Rham representations are potentially semistable.

records.title: Prismatic Dieudonné Theory
records.summary: Prismatic Dieudonné Theory. Classifies $p$-divisible groups over quasi-syntomic rings by admissible prismatic Dieudonné crystals, generalizing crystalline Dieudonné theory.
records.content: Prismatic Dieudonné Theory. Classifies $p$-divisible groups over quasi-syntomic rings by admissible prismatic Dieudonné crystals, generalizing crystalline Dieudonné theory.

records.title: Foundations for Almost Ring Theory
records.summary: Foundations for Almost Ring Theory. Systematic treatment of almost mathematics: almost modules, almost algebras, almost étale extensions and descent, as used in Faltings' approach to $p$-adic Hodge theory.
records.content: Foundations for Almost Ring Theory. Systematic treatment of almost mathematics: almost modules, almost algebras, almost étale extensions and descent, as used in Faltings' approach to $p$-adic Hodge theory.

records.title: Algebraization and Tannaka Duality
records.summary: Algebraization and Tannaka Duality. Proves that for affine $X$, maps $\operatorname{Spf} A \to X$ from complete noetherian rings algebraize, via a Tannaka duality for perfect complexes on qcqs schemes.
records.content: Algebraization and Tannaka Duality. Proves that for affine $X$, maps $\operatorname{Spf} A \to X$ from complete noetherian rings algebraize, via a Tannaka duality for perfect complexes on qcqs schemes.

records.title: Proof of the Geometric Langlands Conjecture I: Construction of the Functor
records.summary: Proof of the Geometric Langlands Conjecture I: Construction of the Functor. Constructs the geometric Langlands functor from the automorphic category $\mathrm{D\text{-}mod}_{\frac12}(\mathrm{Bun}_G)$ to $\mathrm{IndCoh}_{\mathrm{Nilp}}(\mathrm{LocSys}_{\check G})$ and shows the de Rham, Betti, restricted and tempered forms of the conjecture are equivalent.
records.content: Proof of the Geometric Langlands Conjecture I: Construction of the Functor. Constructs the geometric Langlands functor from the automorphic category $\mathrm{D\text{-}mod}_{\frac12}(\mathrm{Bun}_G)$ to $\mathrm{IndCoh}_{\mathrm{Nilp}}(\mathrm{LocSys}_{\check G})$ and shows the de Rham, Betti, restricted and tempered forms of the conjecture are equivalent.

records.title: Periods and Harmonic Analysis on Spherical Varieties
records.summary: Periods and Harmonic Analysis on Spherical Varieties. Develops Plancherel formulas for spherical varieties $X = H \backslash G$ over local fields and formulates conjectures relating global $H$-periods to special values of L-functions determined by the dual group $\check G_X$.
records.content: Periods and Harmonic Analysis on Spherical Varieties. Develops Plancherel formulas for spherical varieties $X = H \backslash G$ over local fields and formulates conjectures relating global $H$-periods to special values of L-functions determined by the dual group $\check G_X$.

records.title: Symplectic Local Root Numbers, Central Critical L-Values, and Restriction Problems
records.summary: Symplectic Local Root Numbers, Central Critical L-Values, and Restriction Problems. States the Gan–Gross–Prasad conjectures on branching laws for classical groups in terms of symplectic root numbers of Langlands parameters, and their global analogue relating period integrals to central L-values.
records.content: Symplectic Local Root Numbers, Central Critical L-Values, and Restriction Problems. States the Gan–Gross–Prasad conjectures on branching laws for classical groups in terms of symplectic root numbers of Langlands parameters, and their global analogue relating period integrals to central L-values.

records.title: Le Lemme Fondamental pour les Algèbres de Lie
records.summary: Le Lemme Fondamental pour les Algèbres de Lie. Proves the fundamental lemma of Langlands–Shelstad using the cohomology of the Hitchin fibration, perverse sheaves, the decomposition theorem and a support theorem for abelian fibrations.
records.content: Le Lemme Fondamental pour les Algèbres de Lie. Proves the fundamental lemma of Langlands–Shelstad using the cohomology of the Hitchin fibration, perverse sheaves, the decomposition theorem and a support theorem for abelian fibrations.

records.title: Chtoucas pour les Groupes Réductifs et Paramétrisation de Langlands Globale
records.summary: Chtoucas pour les Groupes Réductifs et Paramétrisation de Langlands Globale. Constructs the automorphic-to-Galois direction of global Langlands for any reductive group over a function field using excursion operators on the cohomology of moduli of shtukas.
records.content: Chtoucas pour les Groupes Réductifs et Paramétrisation de Langlands Globale. Constructs the automorphic-to-Galois direction of global Langlands for any reductive group over a function field using excursion operators on the cohomology of moduli of shtukas.

records.title: The Conjectural Connections Between Automorphic Representations and Galois Representations
records.summary: The Conjectural Connections Between Automorphic Representations and Galois Representations. Formulates $C$-algebraic and $L$-algebraic automorphic representations and states precise conjectures attaching Galois representations valued in the C-group to algebraic automorphic representations.
records.content: The Conjectural Connections Between Automorphic Representations and Galois Representations. Formulates $C$-algebraic and $L$-algebraic automorphic representations and states precise conjectures attaching Galois representations valued in the C-group to algebraic automorphic representations.

records.title: Modularity Lifting Beyond the Taylor–Wiles Method
records.summary: Modularity Lifting Beyond the Taylor–Wiles Method. Extends Taylor–Wiles patching to settings where the defect $\ell_0 > 0$, proving minimal modularity lifting for weight-one forms and, conditionally, for $\mathrm{GL}_n$ over CM fields.
records.content: Modularity Lifting Beyond the Taylor–Wiles Method. Extends Taylor–Wiles patching to settings where the defect $\ell_0 > 0$, proving minimal modularity lifting for weight-one forms and, conditionally, for $\mathrm{GL}_n$ over CM fields.

records.title: Potential Automorphy over CM Fields
records.summary: Potential Automorphy over CM Fields. Proves potential automorphy of elliptic curves over CM fields and the Ramanujan conjecture on average via local-global compatibility for torsion classes and a new Taylor–Wiles patching argument.
records.content: Potential Automorphy over CM Fields. Proves potential automorphy of elliptic curves over CM fields and the Ramanujan conjecture on average via local-global compatibility for torsion classes and a new Taylor–Wiles patching argument.

records.title: On the Rigid Cohomology of Certain Shimura Varieties
records.summary: On the Rigid Cohomology of Certain Shimura Varieties. Constructs Galois representations for regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representations of $\mathrm{GL}_n$ over CM fields via $p$-adic interpolation on unitary Shimura varieties.
records.content: On the Rigid Cohomology of Certain Shimura Varieties. Constructs Galois representations for regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representations of $\mathrm{GL}_n$ over CM fields via $p$-adic interpolation on unitary Shimura varieties.

records.title: An Introduction to Affine Grassmannians and the Geometric Satake Equivalence
records.summary: An Introduction to Affine Grassmannians and the Geometric Satake Equivalence. Lecture notes on affine Grassmannians, their Schubert varieties, the convolution product and the geometric Satake equivalence $\mathrm{Perv}_{L^+G}(\mathrm{Gr}_G) \simeq \mathrm{Rep}(\check G)$, including mixed-characteristic versions.
records.content: An Introduction to Affine Grassmannians and the Geometric Satake Equivalence. Lecture notes on affine Grassmannians, their Schubert varieties, the convolution product and the geometric Satake equivalence $\mathrm{Perv}_{L^+G}(\mathrm{Gr}_G) \simeq \mathrm{Rep}(\check G)$, including mixed-characteristic versions.

records.title: Geometric Langlands Duality and Representations of Algebraic Groups over Commutative Rings
records.summary: Geometric Langlands Duality and Representations of Algebraic Groups over Commutative Rings. Proves the geometric Satake equivalence with integral coefficients, identifying $L^+G$-equivariant perverse sheaves on the affine Grassmannian with representations of the dual group scheme over any commutative ring.
records.content: Geometric Langlands Duality and Representations of Algebraic Groups over Commutative Rings. Proves the geometric Satake equivalence with integral coefficients, identifying $L^+G$-equivariant perverse sheaves on the affine Grassmannian with representations of the dual group scheme over any commutative ring.

records.title: Electric-Magnetic Duality and the Geometric Langlands Program
records.summary: Electric-Magnetic Duality and the Geometric Langlands Program. Derives geometric Langlands from S-duality of topologically twisted $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang–Mills theory compactified on a Riemann surface, with 't Hooft operators acting as Hecke operators on branes in the Hitchin moduli space.
records.content: Electric-Magnetic Duality and the Geometric Langlands Program. Derives geometric Langlands from S-duality of topologically twisted $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang–Mills theory compactified on a Riemann surface, with 't Hooft operators acting as Hecke operators on branes in the Hitchin moduli space.

records.title: Singular Support of Coherent Sheaves and the Geometric Langlands Conjecture
records.summary: Singular Support of Coherent Sheaves and the Geometric Langlands Conjecture. Introduces singular support for ind-coherent sheaves on quasi-smooth derived stacks and uses it to formulate the corrected geometric Langlands conjecture with nilpotent singular support.
records.content: Singular Support of Coherent Sheaves and the Geometric Langlands Conjecture. Introduces singular support for ind-coherent sheaves on quasi-smooth derived stacks and uses it to formulate the corrected geometric Langlands conjecture with nilpotent singular support.

records.title: On Some Finiteness Questions for Algebraic Stacks
records.summary: On Some Finiteness Questions for Algebraic Stacks. Proves compact generation of $\mathrm{QCoh}$ and D-modules on QCA stacks, and that $\mathrm{D\text{-}mod}(\mathrm{Bun}_G)$ is compactly generated via truncatable open substacks.
records.content: On Some Finiteness Questions for Algebraic Stacks. Proves compact generation of $\mathrm{QCoh}$ and D-modules on QCA stacks, and that $\mathrm{D\text{-}mod}(\mathrm{Bun}_G)$ is compactly generated via truncatable open substacks.

records.title: The Motivic Fundamental Group of $\mathbb{P}^1 \setminus \{0,1,\infty\}$ and the Theorem of Siegel
records.summary: The Motivic Fundamental Group of $\mathbb{P}^1 \setminus \{0,1,\infty\}$ and the Theorem of Siegel. Introduces unipotent Selmer varieties and a non-abelian Chabauty method, reproving Siegel's finiteness of integral points on $\mathbb{P}^1 \setminus \{0,1,\infty\}$.
records.content: The Motivic Fundamental Group of $\mathbb{P}^1 \setminus \{0,1,\infty\}$ and the Theorem of Siegel. Introduces unipotent Selmer varieties and a non-abelian Chabauty method, reproving Siegel's finiteness of integral points on $\mathbb{P}^1 \setminus \{0,1,\infty\}$.

records.title: The Unipotent Albanese Map and Selmer Varieties for Curves
records.summary: The Unipotent Albanese Map and Selmer Varieties for Curves. Develops the unipotent Albanese map from a curve to its Selmer varieties and gives conditions under which Chabauty–Kim proves finiteness of rational points.
records.content: The Unipotent Albanese Map and Selmer Varieties for Curves. Develops the unipotent Albanese map from a curve to its Selmer varieties and gives conditions under which Chabauty–Kim proves finiteness of rational points.

records.title: Explicit Chabauty–Kim for the Split Cartan Modular Curve of Level 13
records.summary: Explicit Chabauty–Kim for the Split Cartan Modular Curve of Level 13. Uses quadratic Chabauty to determine the rational points of the genus-3 modular curve $X_s(13)$, completing the classification of split Cartan images mod 13.
records.content: Explicit Chabauty–Kim for the Split Cartan Modular Curve of Level 13. Uses quadratic Chabauty to determine the rational points of the genus-3 modular curve $X_s(13)$, completing the classification of split Cartan images mod 13.

records.title: Diophantine Problems and p-Adic Period Mappings
records.summary: Diophantine Problems and p-Adic Period Mappings. Proves finiteness of $S$-integral points on hypersurfaces and reproves Mordell's conjecture using big monodromy of variations of Hodge structure and $p$-adic period maps.
records.content: Diophantine Problems and p-Adic Period Mappings. Proves finiteness of $S$-integral points on hypersurfaces and reproves Mordell's conjecture using big monodromy of variations of Hodge structure and $p$-adic period maps.

records.title: Binary Quartic Forms Having Bounded Invariants, and the Boundedness of the Average Rank of Elliptic Curves
records.summary: Binary Quartic Forms Having Bounded Invariants, and the Boundedness of the Average Rank of Elliptic Curves. Counts $\mathrm{PGL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$-orbits of binary quartic forms to show the average size of the 2-Selmer group of elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q}$ is 3, bounding the average rank by 1.5.

records.title: Ternary Cubic Forms Having Bounded Invariants, and the Existence of a Positive Proportion of Elliptic Curves Having Rank 0
records.summary: Ternary Cubic Forms Having Bounded Invariants, and the Existence of a Positive Proportion of Elliptic Curves Having Rank 0. Computes the average size of 3-Selmer groups as 4 and deduces that the average rank is below 1.17 and a positive proportion of elliptic curves have rank 0.

records.title: Thinking Clearly Is a Job, Not a Look
records.summary: A description is clear when it does the job the thinker needs done, and deciding, explaining, and discovering ask for different jobs.
records.content:
A clear thought is usually pictured as one thing: a description with the fog
removed. Unambiguous. Confident. Simple. Unemotional. That picture is a useful
first approximation, and it is the one most advice about thinking assumes. It
also breaks as soon as you notice a sentence that is unambiguous and useless, or
a rough sketch that answers exactly the question you had.

The picture hides the question that decides the answer: clear *to do what?*

When I call a thought clear, I am grading a representation — a sentence, a
diagram, a model, a plan — by whether it serves the task it is being used for.
Drop the task and the word has no standard left to meet. A subway map is clear
for planning a route because it throws away distance and true geography. A
survey map is clear for measuring a plot because it keeps them. Neither map is
the clearer one; they are clear for different jobs.

Most disagreements about whether something is clear are really disagreements
about the job. Three jobs are common enough to name.

## Deciding

A representation used to choose is clear when it separates the actions you can
actually take and preserves the signal that would tell you the choice was wrong.
Detail is not the measure. A one-line rule of thumb can be clear for choosing if
it ranks your real options; a fifty-page report can be unclear if every option
reads the same.

The characteristic failure is a description that is easy to read and leaves the
options indistinguishable. Ease of reading is not nothing — it comes from
familiar words, short sentences, and a shape you have seen before — but none of
those are produced by fit to the decision. They are produced by fluency, and
fluency is a poor gauge of whether the description kept what your choice needs.

## Explaining

A representation used to explain is clear when a listener can rebuild cases you
did not cover. The test is not whether they can repeat the sentences back. Ask
them to answer a question you never answered. If they can, the description
carried the structure rather than the wording. If they can only echo you, they
learned a look.

## Discovering

A representation used to find something new is clear when it can be wrong. It
has to name what would count against it. A model that cannot be contradicted
cannot be corrected, however tidy it is.

This is the job where a fuzzy statement sometimes beats a sharp one. A question
posed too precisely can close off the case that did not fit, and the case that
did not fit is often the one worth finding. The discomfort of not knowing which
category a case belongs to is information when the available categories cut
across it: the unease is the boundary showing through. The honest move is to say
which distinction the categories lose — not to force the case into the nearest
bin.

Not all confusion is insight, though. "It's complicated" explains nothing;
neither does "emergence" or "a skill issue" when used as a label. If the cause is
unknown, say which piece is missing. If a mechanism is available, give it.

## The old picture, revised

"Seeing things as they are" is not wrong, it is underspecified. It survives as
informal shorthand for a common case: you want a description other people can
trust without knowing your private purpose. That is why "neutral" and "unbiased"
feel like synonyms for clear. For that job, stripping the teller's preferences
out is real work and the right work. For choosing under a deadline, or for
noticing what everyone else has smoothed over, that same stripping can remove
the very thing the job needed.

The precise version is narrower and more useful: clarity is a fit between a
representation and a stated job. The shorthand survives because the sharing job
is common. It should not be allowed to stand in for the rest.

## A label to stop using

When "you're not thinking clearly" arrives after someone disagrees, the
definition has been stretched to protect a conclusion. If clarity means
agreement with the speaker, the boundary is doing rhetorical work. The label can
still be fair — but only with the job named and the failure stated. "Your plan
does not distinguish two options you can't both take" is a claim that can be
checked. "You're confused" is not.

## One decision is not a rule

A blunt summary that settled one meeting shows that this decision needed few
distinctions. It is not evidence that bluntness is a rule. The temptation to
generalize from a single success is strongest exactly where the reasoning is
thinnest.

## What to do with this

When a question feels stuck, the work is often not more thinking but naming the
job. Write the answer to "what is this description for?" and check it with one
small test:

- For a decision: list the live options and one observation that would flip
  their order.
- For an explanation: ask someone to work a case you did not mention.
- For discovery: write the sentence that would be false if the idea were wrong.

This is worth trying because a description whose job was never named has no way
to fail, and so no way to be fixed. It is not a guarantee: some questions are
unresolved because the evidence is not in yet, and a clearer question does not
manufacture an answer.

Clarity is not a state to reach and keep. It is a relationship between a
description and a use, and the use can change. Ask what the thought is for, and
"is this clear?" becomes answerable — not everywhere, but exactly where you
need it.

records.title: Mac Set Up
records.summary: A reproducible Mac set up with nix-darwin, Home Manager and a pinned flake
records.content:
# Macintosh

A small, terminal-first Mac setup, declared in code.

The whole machine is described by a Nix flake in my private dotfiles
repository, in the style of
[kunchenguid/dotfiles-mac-nix](https://github.com/kunchenguid/dotfiles-mac-nix):
[nix-darwin](https://github.com/nix-darwin/nix-darwin) for the system,
[Home Manager](https://github.com/nix-community/home-manager) for my user, and
declarative Homebrew for the few GUI apps that are not in nixpkgs. A short
bootstrap script, `setup/mac.sh`, does the handful of things that have to
happen before Nix can take over.

## Why Nix

The previous version of this post was a list of commands, later a script that
ran them. Both describe *how* to reach a state, and both drift: `brew install`
gives whatever is newest that day, and every hand-written dotfile is a second
copy of something a tool could generate.

The flake describes *what* the machine is. `flake.lock` pins nixpkgs,
nix-darwin and Home Manager to exact commits on the 26.05 release branches, so
two Macs built from the same commit get the same packages, versions and
generated config files. Nothing changes until I run `nix flake update` and
commit the new lock. A bad change is one `sudo darwin-rebuild --rollback`
away.

## What owns what

```
nix/host.nix   machine (nix-darwin): Homebrew casks, macOS defaults,
               firewall, Touch ID for sudo
nix/user.nix   user (Home Manager): CLI tools, coding agents, zsh, Git,
               gh, SSH, mise, VS Code and its extensions, ~/src ~/data ~/tmp
files/         configs I edit by hand, linked into $HOME
               (Neovim, Alacritty, tmux, VS Code settings)
setup/mac.sh   the bootstrap
```

The rule of thumb for adding a tool:

- a CLI tool, font or coding agent goes in `home.packages`;
- a GUI app that nixpkgs does not package well goes in `homebrew.casks`;
- a tool with a Home Manager module is configured through `programs.<tool>`,
  not a hand-written file;
- only a file I actually edit by hand lives in `files/`.

## macOS security basics

nix-darwin turns on the firewall (with stealth mode), Touch ID for `sudo`, and
automatic macOS updates. FileVault cannot be declared, so it stays manual:
System Settings → Privacy & Security → FileVault.

## Install

```
git clone <dotfiles-repo> ~/dotfiles
bash ~/dotfiles/setup/mac.sh
```

The checkout must be at `~/dotfiles`, because the files under `files/` are
linked to it directly: an edit to `init.lua` applies without a rebuild. The
script refuses to run anywhere else, as root, or off macOS.

`setup/mac.sh` runs in one pass, and every step is skipped when its work is
already done:

```
xcode      xcode-select --install, then wait for the dialog
nix        the Determinate Nix installer, then source Nix into this shell
homebrew   the Homebrew installer (nix-darwin installs the casks with it)
activate   the first nix-darwin + Home Manager activation
herdr      the herdr installer, then its claude and codex integrations
ssh        ssh-keygen, with a passphrase you type
skills     gh repo clone yujieteo/skills ~/src/skills, once gh is signed in
```

rather than from whatever `master` is today:

```
  switch --flake ~/dotfiles#mac
```

renamed with a `.backup` suffix rather than deleted.

```
claude-code codex opencode

```
